Conselice, Pratika Dayal, Qinyue Fei, Andreas L. Faisst Jeyhan S. Kartaltepe, Paulo A. A. Lopes, Ray A. Lucas, Georgios E. Magdis, Nicholas S. Martis, Casey Papovich, Daniel Schaerer, Francesco Valentino, Eros Vanzella, Joseph F. V. Allingham, Norman A. Grogin, Mauro Gonz\'alez-Otero, Massimo Ricotti, Rogier A. Windhorst

papers.title: Evolution and afterglow emission of gamma-ray burst jets from binary neutron star mergers
papers.summary: Relativistic jets launched in binary neutron star (BNS) mergers are widely accepted as the engines powering most of the population of short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Understanding their structure and dynamics-particularly during and after breakout from the merger ejecta-is crucial for interpreting GRB afterglows, especially for off-axis observers. Traditional models often assume simple angular or radial jet profiles, potentially missing key features emerging for jets piercing through realistic environments. This work aims to investigate the formation and evolution of the jet structure as it propagates through a non-homogeneous, anisotropic BNS merger environment. We focus on how the interaction with the ambient medium shapes the jet's angular and velocity distributions and assess the impact of this realistic structure on the resulting afterglow light curves. We perform a series of 3D relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of jets launched in post-merger environments, exploring different injection conditions. Simulations are evolved to late times, approaching the ballistic regime, where further dynamical evolution becomes negligible. From the resulting outflows, we extract energy and velocity profiles and compute multi-wavelength afterglow light curves using a semi-analytic model that includes radial stratification and the full 3D jet geometry. More energetic or earlier-launched jets drill more efficiently through the ejecta, but all develop asymmetries that leave clear imprints in the off-axis afterglow light curves. All models exhibit a complex multi-shock breakout structure responsible for an early, dimmer peak in the afterglow. Despite structural differences, all simulated jets are consistent with the observational data of the multi-messenger BNS merger event GW170817.

authors.name: Emma Dreas, Om Sharan Salafia, Andrea Pavan, Riccardo Ciolfi, Annalisa Celotti

papers.title: Low-$T/|W|$ instabilities in differentially rotating neutron stars resembling merger remnants
papers.summary: We construct constant rest-mass sequences of equilibrium models of differentially rotating neutron stars which resemble binary neutron star post-merger remnants. For a more realistic description of the post-merger remnant, we impose that each model carries approximately $95\%$ of the angular momentum that a binary system with the same total rest-mass has at the moment of merging, based on an empirical relation informed from neutron star merger simulations. We account for equation of state effects by employing two distinct microphysical descriptions for high density matter. We dynamically evolve the equilibrium models with a three-dimensional general relativistic hydrodynamics code that employs the conformal flatness approximation. We investigate the connection between the occurrence of the instability and the existence of corotation radii within the stellar configurations and determine the instability window for both equation of state sequences. The occurrence of low-$T/|W|$ instabilities leads to pronounced gravitational wave emission in the range $0.13 \lessapprox\beta \lessapprox 0.2$, while models outside this range exhibit less pronounced features in the gravitational wave spectrum. The prominence of gravitational wave emission is primarily determined by $\beta$, while the equation of state seems to have a more minor effect. We present correlations between the strength of the gravitational wave emission associated with the instability and properties of the equilibrium models. Stellar configurations modelled by different equations of state display differences in the timescales over which the various dynamical features develop, as well as whether they exhibit a pronounced $m=1$ deformation. Potential relations between the instability growth timescales and properties of the stellar models are studied.

authors.name: Georgios Lioutas, Panagiotis Iosif, Andreas Bauswein, Nikolaos Stergioulas

papers.title: Blueshifted lines from the inner accretion disc's rotation can explain quasar absorption "forests"
papers.summary: Recent XRISM observations of active galactic nuclei (AGN) such as PDS 456 have revealed ``forests'' of absorption lines best modeled by five distinct absorption zones with varying large blueshifts. We propose a model in which these relativistic blueshifts originate from the motion of the accretion disc itself, rather than from a clumpy super-Eddington outflow at hundreds of gravitational radii $r_g\equiv GM/c^2$. We demonstrate that thin fragments of absorbing material lying just above the accretion disc at varying radii can produce the observed energy shifts and separations of the absorption zones. In this model, the PDS 456 X-ray transmission spectrum is well reproduced by fragments of azimuthal rings with radial widths $\Delta r\lesssim1r_g$ at locations between the black hole's innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and $\approx15r_g$. This model suggests that the absorption forests seen in XRISM observations can probe the surface structure of the innermost ($\lesssim15r_g$) regions of quasar accretion discs and predicts the presence of redshifted absorbers.

authors.name: Amelia M. Hankla, Fergus J. E. Baker, Daniel R. Wilkins, Andrew C. Fabian

papers.title: Cosmological Impact of Redshift-Dependent Type Ia Supernovae Calibration
papers.summary: Type Ia supernovae (SNIa) play a central role in constraining the late-time expansion history of the Universe and are directly implicated in current cosmological tensions. Motivated by the possibility of unaccounted redshift-dependent calibration systematics or new physics, we investigate the impact of a phenomenological correction to SNIa magnitudes that scales with cosmic look-back time. We parameterize this effect with a free amplitude and constrain it using a combination of cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and SNIa data, considering both $\Lambda$CDM and dynamical dark energy models. Importantly, our parameterization is not intended to serve as a proxy for SNIa progenitor age, as current observations show no significant difference in standardized SNIa brightness between young and old progenitor populations at low redshift. We find no evidence for a redshift-dependent calibration effect when fitting uncalibrated SNIa data, and its inclusion has a negligible impact on cosmological parameters within $\Lambda$CDM, nor does it qualitatively change the inferred dynamics of evolving dark energy. When incorporating a prior on the SNIa absolute magnitude from SH0ES, a nonzero calibration parameter is weakly preferred within $\Lambda$CDM. Interestingly, with dynamical dark energy, the preference of a nonzero calibration parameter increases to $4.3\sigma$, and it can accommodate both the distance ladder and early-Universe constraints, reducing the Hubble tension to $1.5\sigma$, with the best-fit model effectively corresponding to a constant equation of state with $w < -1$. Overall, our results indicate that redshift-dependent SNIa calibration effects, as parameterized here, are not supported by current data within $\Lambda$CDM, but can play a role in reconciling cosmological datasets when combined with extensions to the late-time expansion history.

authors.name: Seyed Hamidreza Mirpoorian, Meng-Xiang Lin, Levon Pogosian

papers.title: Dimming and pulsation shock of the coalesced star V838 Monocerotis
papers.summary: V838 Mon is the remnant of a 2002 stellar merger. Currently it closely resembles a red supergiant, but its luminosity is sustained by core H burning and continued contraction toward hydrostatic equilibrium. In late 2025, the system entered the deepest dimming event observed since 2006. We characterize the dimming event of V838 Mon using multiband photometry and high-resolution spectroscopy spanning from the dimming minimum through the recovery phase. We obtained $UBVRI JHK_s$ photometry with the NOT telescope and extracted light curves from the public AAVSO, ATLAS, ZTF, and ASAS-SN databases. These data were supplemented by time-series spectra acquired with SALT/HRS, LBT/PEPSI, VLT/Xshooter, and VLT/UVES, covering the spectral range 3760-24 800 A at resolutions $R$=6700-130 000.The photometric color evolution during the dimming can be well reproduced by grey dust extinction with $A_V$ = 1.3 mag, consistent with a transiting clump of freshly formed circumstellar dust. The photospheric effective temperature changed by no more than ~200 K during the event. During the recovery phase, H recombination lines from Balmer, Paschen, and Brackett series appeared in emission. Their line ratios do not follow Case B but are reminiscent of H emission in pulsating M-type miras near maximum light. These features are interpreted as arising from a pulsation shock propagating outward from below the photosphere. Simultaneously, low-ionization metal lines appeared blueshifted by 90 km\s relative to the stellar rest frame, tracing shock-accelerated gas on the near side of the stellar disk. The spectroscopic sequence suggests that the 2026 dimming was itself triggered by a preceding pulsation shock that occurred earlier in 2025. The observed shock may trigger a subsequent dimming event later in 2026.

authors.name: T. Kami\'nski (CAMK Toru\'n), C. E. Woodward (Minnesota Institute of Astrophysics), T. Liimets (Tartu Observatory), M. R. Schmidt (CAMK Toru\'n), A. A. Djupvik (NOT, Aarhus University), I. Ilyin (Leibniz-Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam)

papers.title: Steady-state Stellar Winds Driven by Recombination
papers.summary: Hydrogen and helium recombination energy has been proposed as a potential driver of mass ejection in common-envelope evolution and other eruptive stellar phenomena. We investigate whether recombination can by itself launch a steady, transonic wind from near a stellar surface. Using a tabulated equation of state, we explore steady-state, adiabatic wind solutions over a broad range of stellar mass, density, and temperature. We classify a wind as recombination-driven only if the gas is gravitationally bound prior to recombination and if the released energy remains trapped until the flow becomes unbound. Only a small subset of the transonic solutions satisfies both conditions. In most cases, the gas is either already unbound without recombination or loses the released energy through radiative diffusion while still bound. The remaining candidate solutions require substantial outflow velocities of order $\gtrsim10\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ at $10\,R_\odot$ and mass-loss rates $\sim 0.1$-$10\,\rm M_\odot/yr$, which would rapidly deplete the stellar envelope. We conclude that, within our adiabatic framework and subject to an a posteriori radiative-trapping criterion, recombination energy alone is unlikely to launch a steady wind from a hydrostatic envelope. It can, however, accelerate and unbind a pre-existing outflow generated by processes such as binary orbital decay.

authors.name: Eritas Yang, Eliot Quataert

papers.title: MSA-3D: Rotation Curves and Dark Matter Fractions at z~0.5-1.7 with JWST/NIRSpec
papers.summary: We present rotation curves and inner mass distributions for 30 star-forming galaxies at $0.5<z<1.7$, down to stellar masses of $\sim10^9\,M_\odot$, observed with JWST/NIRSpec in the MSA-3D Cycle 1 survey. We combine spatially resolved ionised-gas kinematics and JWST/NIRCam imaging in forward dynamical models to constrain baryonic and dark matter contributions. The 24 golden-sample galaxies exhibit ordered rotation, with intrinsic dispersions of $\sigma_0\simeq34$--63~km\,s$^{-1}$ and median $V_{\rm rot}/\sigma_0=2.9$ at $2.2R_{\rm s}$. Their stellar Tully--Fisher relation has a slope consistent with previous $z\sim1$ studies ($a=3.8\pm0.5$) but substantial inter-survey differences in normalisation. Within the disk effective radius, we obtain a median dark matter fraction $f_{\rm DM}(R_e)=0.73$ (68\% range: 0.49--0.84), with systematic dependence on the adopted baryonic mass scale. Across comparison surveys, $f_{\rm DM}(R_e)$ correlates more strongly with baryonic surface density than stellar mass, although neither trend is significant within MSA-3D. Five galaxies favour inner halo slopes shallower than NFW (versus $\approx2$ expected by chance), three significantly in model-matched NFW injection tests. Among 16 galaxies with sufficient radial coverage, five have rising, eight flat, and three falling rotation curves (although individual slopes are mostly not significant), with no clear dependence on other properties. Together, these results indicate that these low-mass disks at $z\sim1$ are dark-matter dominated within $R_e$ for the baryonic mass scale favoured by the kinematics, although adopting the catalogue-based masses lowers the median to $\approx0.5$. Their inner halo profiles are generally consistent with or moderately shallower than NFW. These observations demonstrate the efficiency of JWST for extending resolved dynamical studies to lower-mass galaxies.

authors.name: Juan M. Espejo Salcedo, Danail Obreschkow, Karl Glazebrook, Tucker Jones, Ivana Bari\v{s}i\'c, Natascha M. F\"orster Schreiber, Takafumi Tsukui, Xin Wang, Mengting Ju, Qianqiao Zhou, Amit Nestor-Schachar, Ryan L. Sanders, Stavros Pastras, Namrata Roy, Alaina Henry, Kyle Westfall, Themiya Nanayakkara, Matthew Malkan, Fahmi M. Al Farisy, Isaac Kanowski

papers.title: Compaction function in stochastic inflation: a FOREST of type I and II primordial black holes
papers.summary: We show how to compute the compaction function within stochastic inflation, by solving the random field dynamics on stochastic binary trees. In this framework, the compaction function is directly related to the ratio of the volumes emerging from the sibling and child branches of a given node. This construction also determines whether or not the areal radius of a perturbation increases monotonically with the radial coordinate, thereby distinguishing between type-I and type-II fluctuations. As an application, we investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation in a single-field toy model with a constant potential slope, using stochastic-tree realizations generated with the public code FOREST. In the classical regime, where quantum diffusion is subdominant, the PBH mass function is narrowly distributed and type-II fluctuations are strongly suppressed relative to type I. By contrast, in the quantum and near-critical (i.e. close to eternal inflation) regimes, the PBH mass distribution spans several orders of magnitude, the overall PBH abundance is enhanced, and type-II fluctuations outnumber type I. In that case cloud-in-cloud effects are also important, highlighting the need for a better understanding of the evolution and collapse of type-II fluctuations in order to obtain robust PBH predictions when stochastic effects are significant.

authors.name: Chiara Animali, Pierre Auclair, Baptiste Blachier, Eemeli Tomberg, Vincent Vennin

papers.title: Low-hard to high-soft spectral state transitions in the faintest early-X-ray-detected optical tidal disruption event TDE 2025aarm
papers.summary: We report the X-ray and optical spectroscopic properties of TDE 2025aarm, the second closest tidal disruption event (TDE) discovered to date. The proximity of this source, combined with a deep and intense X-ray monitoring campaign spanning six months, allowed us to probe the source down to an unprecedented 0.2-10 keV luminosity of $\sim7\times10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$ close to the optical peak. This renders TDE 2025aarm the faintest early-X-ray-detected TDE to date. After the first X-ray detection, the source brightened by nearly two orders of magnitude, reaching a peak luminosity of $\sim5\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ about four months after the optical peak. Through time-resolved X-ray spectral analysis, we find that TDE 2025aarm evolved from an initially hard, power-law-dominated X-ray state into a softer, disk-dominated state as the luminosity increased, before hardening again at later times. Such low-hard-to-high-soft state transitions are commonly observed in black hole X-ray binaries (XRBs) but have not previously been reported in thermal TDEs. We show that the spectral evolution can be described by variations in the relative contributions of an accretion disk and a Comptonizing component, qualitatively resembling the disk--corona evolution observed in XRBs. We also present the results of our optical spectroscopic follow-up campaign with HET/LRS2, confirming the TDE classification and revealing NIII Bowen fluorescence features. The extremely faint early-time X-ray emission of TDE 2025aarm further supports the idea that the historical dichotomy between X-ray-bright and X-ray-undetected TDEs is largely driven by selection effects related to the depth, cadence, and duration of X-ray follow-up observations. TDE 2025aarm therefore provides new insight into both the accretion physics of TDEs and the possible universality of accretion across several orders of magnitude in black hole mass.

authors.name: Pietro Baldini, Arne Rau, Andrea Merloni, Jean Somalwar, Se\'an J. Brennan, Elias Kyritsis, Hannah C. I. Wichern, Peter Boorman, Panos Charalampopoulos, Lixin Dai, Gaurava K. Jaisawal, Chichuan Jin, Tianying Lian, Kirpal Nandra

papers.title: From Multimessenger Inference to Simulations: A Ranked Ensemble of Finite-Temperature Equations of State
papers.summary: We construct a set of microphysical, finite-temperature equations of state (EOSs) for numerical simulations of neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae that is consistent with modern constraints from nuclear theory and multimessenger astronomy and systematically spans the posterior distribution of allowed EOSs. The EOSs are based on a simplified Skyrme functional whose inputs are nuclear matter saturation properties, extended to supra-saturation densities through the speed of sound at a set of reference densities. The models are assigned continuous likelihood weights from chiral effective field theory and perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations, the gravitational-wave signal GW170817, and four NICER mass-radius measurements. From the resulting catalog of 3.6 million EOSs, the posterior yields $R_{1.4} = 11.8^{+0.8}_{-0.7}$ km, $\Lambda_{1.4} = 342^{+181}_{-118}$, and $M_{\rm max}^{\rm TOV} = 2.17^{+0.23}_{-0.16}\,M_\odot$ (medians with 90% credible intervals). From this posterior we select a ranked twelve-member ensemble, headed by a fiducial, central EOS, whose members are individually plausible while bracketing the posterior spread of each neutron-star observable. For all ensemble members we generate general-purpose finite-temperature tables with the SROEOS code, each accompanied by nucleon effective-mass variants for systematic studies of thermal effects, to be made publicly available upon publication.

authors.name: Maximilian Jacobi, Giulia Huez, Sebastiano Bernuzzi, David Radice

papers.title: Lunar Reflective Interferometry
papers.summary: We present the method of lunar reflection interferometry (LRI) in which a virtual interferometer can be formed by using a spacecraft-borne antenna in lunar orbit that receives both direct rays and those reflected from the lunar surface. The technique exploits the method of images and is akin to the classic "sea cliff" interferometer, with the Moon's surface, primarily the lunar Maria, replacing the ocean surface. We describe the method in detail, demonstrate that significant portions of the Moon's surface are sufficiently smooth at low radio frequencies, $\nu \lesssim 10\,\mathrm{MHz}$, for the technique to work, and outline a spacecraft instrument implementation. We describe potential systematic errors and how they could be mitigated. We present several astrophysics applications of the method.

authors.name: Peter W. Gorham, T. Joseph W. Lazio, Andrew Romero-Wolf, Patrick S. Allison, Marin M. Anderson, Ali M. Bramson, Roman Burridge, Amy Connolly, Emily S. Costello, Cosmin Deaconu, Susan Lepri, Christian Miki, Eric Oberla, Sean Peters, Kathryn Plant, Julie Rolla, Matthew Siegler

papers.title: Near universality of nonlinear transverse and radial velocity responses in spherical collapse with arbitrary radial profiles
papers.summary: The nonlinear relation between density and expansion is usually formulated for a homogeneous spherical top hat, which has a single local Hubble rate. A smooth spherical profile instead expands differently along and across the radial direction-a direct signature of radial inhomogeneity. We show that, for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise response is nevertheless fixed by one top-hat function. Given the local and enclosed density contrasts, a transverse response and its derivative determine the transverse and radial expansion rates. The linear and second-order limits are algebraic maps whose only dynamical input is the usual growth rate. An exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating an evolution equation. We check that it reconstructs full Lambda-Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi profiles to numerical precision. We also provide a derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit that requires only the growth rate and the local and enclosed density contrasts. Across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations and for a shell located in the compensated transition, the maximum relative errors are 0.3% and 0.7% in the transverse and radial responses, respectively. This compact formulation separates the production of a density profile from its expansion response and makes the effect of radial gradients explicit.

authors.name: Valerio Marra

papers.title: An Outer Giant Excites and Constrains the Orbit of $\pi$ Mensae d
papers.summary: The nearby $\pi$ Mensae system contains the eccentric giant planet b on a 5.7 yr orbit, the 6.27 day transiting sub-Neptune c, and a candidate planet d on a 123 day orbit between them. Published estimates place the eccentricity of d between approximately 0.2 and 0.4. We reanalyze 772 published velocities with three-Keplerian fits and explore three-dimensional b-d dynamics with $N$-body integrations. The high-eccentricity solution persists when the phase or apsidal prior is widened; exact importance reweighting to a population-informed Beta eccentricity prior gives $e_d=0.378^{+0.050}_{-0.049}$. In 20 kyr integrations, 84.5% of configurations near the prograde and retrograde coplanar endpoints survive, compared with 21.3% across $60^\circ\leq I_{bd}<120^\circ$; stellar collisions dominate the failures. Secular forcing by b moves 53 of 62 one-Myr survivors initialized with $e_d\leq0.1$ into $0.3\leq e_d\leq0.5$. Representative b+d configurations remain viable for 100 Myr, whereas controls with c and general relativity retain fewer systems. The outer giant can therefore excite the observed eccentricity of d while constraining its viable orbit toward prograde or retrograde near-coplanar configurations.

authors.name: Qunfeng Jiang

papers.title: Probing Early Phases of the Epoch of Reionization with the $\mathrm{kSZ}^{2}\times21\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ Cross-Correlation
papers.summary: Observations of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) provide key insights into the nature of the first luminous sources and the thermal state of the intergalactic medium (IGM). Cross-correlations between the kinetic Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect and neutral hydrogen (HI) 21-cm emission offer a promising probe of this era, sensitive to both the ionization and thermal histories of the early Universe. We investigate the cross-correlation of the squared kSZ field with the squared 21-cm intensity-mapping field ($\mathrm{kSZ}^{2}\times21\mathrm{cm}^{2}$) over $z\simeq9$--$16$, focusing on the impact of spatial fluctuations in the HI spin temperature. This higher-order statistic avoids line-of-sight cancellations in the kSZ signal, while squaring the 21-cm field enables non-vanishing correlations with pairs of equal and opposite high-$k_\parallel$ modes accessible outside the foreground wedge. We forecast the cumulative signal-to-noise ratio ($\mathrm{S/N}$) for several combinations of 21-cm and CMB experiments, including realistic instrumental noise. For a fiducial heating history and an optimistic foreground-avoidance scenario ($k_\parallel\leq0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$), we find $\mathrm{S/N}\simeq5.89$ for SKA-Low AA$^\ast\times$CMB-HD and $\simeq3.62$ for HERA$\times$CMB-HD. If the foreground wedge extends to the horizon, these decrease to $2.94$ and $2.85$, respectively. {Our results demonstrate that $\mathrm{kSZ}^{2}\times21\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ is sensitive to the ionization structure of the IGM, and, provided that X-ray heating is not too efficient, also to its thermal evolution, providing complementary constraints on the high-redshift thermal and reionization histories.

authors.name: Wen-Qing Guo (Stellenbosch University, South Africa), Yin-Zhe Ma (Stellenbosch University, South Africa), Adam Lidz (University of Pennsylvania, USA), Steven Murray (Stellenbosch University, South Africa), Hemanth Potluri (Stellenbosch University, South Africa)

papers.title: Detailed study of HD 219134: A benchmark K dwarf with a compact planetary system
papers.summary: Space missions such as CoRoT, Kepler, and TESS have transformed asteroseismology and its synergies with exoplanet science. We revisit the nearby K-dwarf HD 219134 to investigate the tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update its fundamental parameters, and reconstruct the rotational, magnetic, and atmospheric evolution of the system. We combine forward asteroseismic modeling with seismic inversions to assess systematics from non-seismic constraints, radius measurements, and surface modeling. The revised stellar properties are then used for rotational evolution, stellar-wind, and high-energy irradiation calculations. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius, while the asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the 2019 interferometric measurement. We obtain $M=0.779\pm0.015_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.006_\mathrm{(sys)}\ M_\odot$, $R=0.753\pm0.005_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.002_\mathrm{(sys)}\ R_\odot$, and an age of $8.92\pm0.89_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.19_\mathrm{(sys)}$ Gyr. These systematics include only non-seismic constraints; literature combined uncertainties from physical inputs and surface effects are $0.007M_\odot$, $0.002R_\odot$, and $0.81$ Gyr. Rotational and wind modelling shows that standard magnetic braking is broadly compatible with the present-day rotation and angular-momentum loss. Weakened braking gives a closer match but challenges standard wind-loss scalings. The inferred X-ray history suggests early stripping of the innermost planets, while the outer planets likely retained part of their primordial envelopes; HD 219134d experienced only moderate erosion. The apparent radius discrepancy likely reflects underestimated uncertainties in previous interferometric analyses rather than an astrophysical inconsistency. We advocate adopting the asteroseismic radius, which is robust to modeling assumptions and optimisation strategies.

authors.name: J\'er\^ome B\'etrisey, Camilla Pezzotti, Ga\"el Buldgen, Aline A. Vidotto, Colin P. Folsom, Micha\"el De Becker, Micha\"el Gillon

papers.title: Thermodynamically consistent equation of state tables for use in giant planet and brown dwarf interior modeling
papers.summary: Equation of state (EOS) tables used in giant planet modeling exhibit regions of strong thermodynamic inconsistency, or disobedience to the first law of thermodynamics. These generally result from smooth interpolation over physical discontinuities or between thermodynamic sub-domains governed by different physical models. The effect of thermodynamic inconsistency on structure models of planets evolved with these EOS has never been studied in detail, although it is understood to introduce spurious sources or sinks of energy or entropy in the models, leading to inaccuracies. Here, we present a method for improving the thermodynamic consistency of an existing EOS table, based on constructing a Helmholtz free energy $F(\rho,T)$ covering the EOS domain and deriving all the other necessary EOS quantities from it. This method produces EOS tables with roughly thousandfold better thermodynamic consistency across the EOS domain of interest, as quantified by three thermodynamic consistency metrics derived from the first law. We also present a controlled experiment comparing giant planet models evolved with MESA using the original EOS and the $F$-derived, thermodynamically consistent versions, and find that the models can differ by up to $5\%$ in radius at an age of 5 Gyr, and by up to $25\%$ in luminosity at earlier stages of evolution; thermodynamic consistency is thus an especially important consideration for characterising young directly imaged planets. We present the $F$-derived, thermodynamically consistent versions of the tables for download at \href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21103561}{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21103561}, along with example MESA inlists to reproduce our evolution models.

authors.name: Emily Sandford, Yamila Miguel

papers.title: The GAPS Programme at TNG LXXXI. The puzzle of the HeI absorption signal in the atmosphere of V1298 Tau b with GIARPS@TNG
papers.summary: Atmospheric escape shapes close-in planets mostly in their first tens of Myr. The young V1298Tau system (10-30Myr) is a benchmark for investigating photoevaporation and planetary evolution at early stages. The metastable HeI near-infrared triplet is a key proxy for atmospheric escape. We aim to detect and characterise HeI in the extended atmosphere of V1298Taub. We analysed four transits over a 4-year baseline using GIARPS (GIANO-B + HARPS-N) at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo. We re-derived the projected spin-orbit angle by modelling the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Using simultaneous optical and near-infrared high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of V1298Taub, we monitored the HeI triplet alongside key chromospheric indicators ($\log R'_{HK}$, H$\alpha$, and NaI) to disentangle stellar activity from planetary evaporation. While the stellar spectra show significant night-to-night variability, transmission spectroscopy reveals persistent HeI absorption across all four epochs. This contrasts with H$\alpha$ and NaI, observed over two nights with simultaneous HARPS-N monitoring, which fluctuate between emission and absorption due to stellar activity. The consistent presence of HeI over 4 years may suggest a planetary origin, despite stellar-driven depth modulation. ATES hydrodynamic simulations show that stellar XUV flux variations modulate the HeI absorption depth and equivalent width. Furthermore, stellar wind fluctuations likely drive the observed night-to-night variability of the exospheric structure. The detection of HeI across all epochs may support planetary evaporation, despite modulation by stellar activity. Our results underscore that disentangling a planetary signal from stellar contamination remains challenging for highly active hosts; securing the planetary nature of the HeI signature requires activity monitoring and full transit coverage to establish a robust baseline.

authors.name: G. Guilluy, J. Orell-Miquel, A. Sozzetti, M. C. D'Arpa, N. Greco, A. F. Lanza, D. Sicilia, A. Caldiroli, R. Spinelli, D. Locci, P. Leonardi, L. Mancini, S. Colombo, M. Rainer, F. Borsa, A. Maggio, A. S. Bonomo, L. Affer, V. Andretta, F. Biassoni, A. Bignamini, W. Boschin, M. Brogi, C. Di Maio, L. Fossati, E. Gallo, F. Haardt, M. L\'opez-Puertas, V. Lorenzi, L. Malavolta, J. Maldonaldo, F. Manni, G. Micela, F. Murgas, V. Nascimbeni, E. Palle, J. Sanz-Forcada, G. Scandariato, J. Southworth, J. Tregloan-Reed

papers.title: The Unusual X-ray Spectrum of R Mon
papers.summary: The optically obscured young star R Mon illuminates Hubble's Variable Nebula and has historically been classified as an intermediate mass pre-main sequence Herbig Be star. We present Chandra observations of R Mon revealing a hard X-ray source viewed through high absorption from circumstellar gas known to be present from previous CO observations. The X-ray spectrum is characterized by line emission from the He-like Fe K complex (6.7 keV) tracing very hot plasma and fluorescent Fe emission (6.4 keV) from cold gas near the star that is irradiated by hard X-rays. Low-level variability on a timescale of less than one day is detected, but no large impulsive flares. The hot plasma and variability cannot be explained by shock models and magnetically confined plasma is inferred. The hard X-ray spectrum of R Mon does not resemble the soft spectra of prototypical Herbig stars but is remarkably similar to some class I protostars such as NGC 2071-IRS 1. As judged by its X-ray and infrared properties, we conclude that R Mon is a class I protostar and thus provides a rare snapshot of an emergent intermediate mass star enveloped in X-ray irradiated gas and dust.

authors.name: Stephen L. Skinner, Manuel Guedel

papers.title: MARTA: An overmassive black hole hidden in a young, clumpy, and metal-poor galaxy at z~3.8
papers.summary: JWST has extended the search for accreting black holes into the high-redshift, low-mass regime. We report a low-mass black hole candidate in MARTA 3887, a clumpy, metal-poor galaxy at $z=3.7694$, combining deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, HST and JWST imaging, and archival VLT/MUSE data. We detect a broad H$\alpha$ component with $L_{\rm H\alpha,b}=2.35\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and FWHM $=1270^{+260}_{-250}$ km s$^{-1}$, with no [O III] counterpart of comparable width. Under a broad-line-region interpretation, virial calibrations give $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.52^{+0.18}_{-0.23}$ and $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=0.07$, or up to 0.38 for alternative calibrations. The host comprises at least three compact clumps, with $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=8.16^{+0.09}_{-0.10}$. If stellar photoionization dominates the narrow lines, the gas is highly ionized and metal poor, with $12+\log({\rm O/H})=7.68\pm0.04$ ($\simeq0.10\,Z_\odot$). The inferred $M_{\rm BH}/M_\star=2.3\%$ lies about 2 dex above the extrapolated local relation, suggesting that black-hole growth has outpaced the assembly of the observed host. If growth began only when the first 10% of the observed stellar mass had formed ($t_{10}=92$ Myr ago), a $10^2\,M_\odot$ seed would require a lifetime-mean Eddington ratio $\simeq5.7$; earlier growth or a more massive, e.g. direct-collapse, seed would allow sub-Eddington mean accretion. MUSE reveals extended Ly$\alpha$ emission ($\simeq6.5$-6.9 proper kpc), offset by $+64^{+10}_{-8}$ km s$^{-1}$ from systemic, with a provisional escape fraction of $\simeq0.44$. Together with a Mg II doublet ratio close to the optically thin limit and a high [O III]/[O II] ratio, this makes MARTA 3887 a laboratory to study black-hole growth, stellar assembly, and ionizing-photon escape jointly.

authors.name: Mirko Curti, Bianca Moreschini, Elisa Cataldi, Francesco Belfiore, Ivan Delvecchio, Sophie Koudmani, Anthony J. Taylor, Alessandro Marconi, Filippo Mannucci, Elena Bertola, Giovanni Cresci, Anna Feltre, Roberto Maiolino, Francesca Pozzi, Letizia Scaloni, Alberto Traina, Caterina Bracci, Stefano Carniani, Carlotta Gruppioni, Giacomo Venturi, Magda Arnaboldi, Meriem Behiri, Michele Ginolfi, Mahsa Kohandel, Livia Vallini

papers.title: On the Detectability of Compact Multi-Planet Systems via Gravitational Microlensing
papers.summary: Compact multi-planet systems orbiting ultracool dwarfs, such as TRAPPIST-1, may be a major population of terrestrial worlds with poorly constrained demographics. Individual close-in planets are expected to escape microlensing detection, but whether a compact system can produce a detectable collective signal remains to be quantified. We calculate the microlensing signal from each TRAPPIST-1 planet, and of all seven combined, if the system were a lens toward the bulge. For a 0.09 $M_\odot$ lens at 4 kpc, $R_E \approx 1.21$ AU, placing the planets at $s = 0.010$--$0.051~\theta_E$, 12--63 times interior to the lensing zone. We measure each signal as the residual after fitting a single-lens model, which accounts for the barycentric dipole. Because the quadrupole term cancels between the two images to first order, the residual scales as the octupole ($q s^3$), reaching $|\delta A / A| \sim 10^{-6}$. The seven planets combined yield $\Delta\chi^2 \sim 10^{-3}$ even at 1~mmag precision, five orders of magnitude below the standard detection threshold. Detection requires increasing all planet masses by a factor of $\sim$300, whereas the resonant chain loses its guarantee of Hill stability at a factor of $\sim$7. Only a lens within $\sim$15 pc of the source or the Sun places the outer planets in the lensing zone. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is therefore not expected to detect a TRAPPIST-1-like system through microlensing, whereas its transit channel in the same fields can detect such planets in large numbers, marking a sharp boundary in the Galactic census between microlensing and transit sensitivity.

authors.name: Stephen R. Kane

papers.title: Constraining Ganymede's Interior Structure and Bulk Composition from Its Present-Day Magnetic Field Strength
papers.summary: Ganymede is the only Solar System satellite with a global magnetic field driven by a core dynamo. Although its small moment-of-inertia (MoI) factor indicates a differentiated structure of a metallic core, rocky mantle, and outer hydrosphere, its exact bulk composition and layer thicknesses remain highly uncertain. We developed a comprehensive, long-term thermochemical evolution model that couples thermal history with magnetic field generation. Building upon previous theoretical frameworks, this study systematically evaluates how diverse chondritic precursor compositions constrain Ganymede's internal thermochemical evolution and core solidification processes. Based on interior structures initially permitted by a wide range of chondritic compositions and geodetic constraints, we applied the observed equatorial surface magnetic field strength ($\sim$719 nT) as a dynamic filter. Our evolutionary simulations demonstrate that while magnetic dynamos can operate under entire melting, Fe-snow, and FeS-layer regimes, the requirement to sustain the observed field strength strongly restricts the viable interior models. Satisfying this constraint preferentially requires a relatively large core radius and a specific, non-eutectic bulk core sulfur concentration. Consequently, this coupled thermochemical approach highlights the main novelty of this study: characterizing the hydrosphere's density serves as an independent constraint to break the structural degeneracy of Ganymede's bulk composition. Our model indicates that L and CI chondrites yield parameter spaces capable of sustaining comparable field strengths under a low-density hydrosphere scenario (1,200 kg m-3), whereas the H chondrite composition can satisfy this criterion under a high-density scenario (1,300 kg m-3). These predictions provide a critical framework to be tested by the JUICE mission arriving in 2031.

authors.name: Jun Kimura, Ryohei Kawakami, Taro Matsuo, Sho Sasaki

papers.title: High precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
papers.summary: Binary millisecond pulsars (MSPs) serve as exceptional astrophysical laboratories for a wide range of astrophysical studies, all of which rely on precise property measurements allowed by pulsar timing. In this paper, we present high-precision timing solutions for seven binary MSPs monitored by the European Pulsar Timing Array. By combining data collected from the five largest radio telescopes in Europe, as well as their coherently combined form, the Large European Array for Pulsars, we achieve phase-coherent timing solutions for all seven pulsars. We conduct a Bayesian timing and noise analysis on the combined data, yielding measurements of astrometric and orbital parameters with broadly improved precision, some reported for the first time. For PSRs J0125-2327, J1741+1351 and J2043+1711, we determine their distances and transverse velocities from astrometric measurements, and infer their masses via Shapiro delay measurements. Additionally, we examine the various contributions to the secular orbital-period variations for PSRs J0125-2327, J1125+7819 and J1741+1351, and estimate their kinematic distances. For PSRs J0125-2327 and J1741+1351, we detect the signature of annual-orbital parallax in the timing data. This allows us to derive a strongly favored, unique solution for the orbital ascending node and inclination angle for PSR J0125-2327, and a tightly constrained ascending node for PSR J1741+1351. Moreover, we use the orbital periods and their derivatives for several binary MSPs to place upper limits on gravitational-wave strain in both the sub-nanohertz and microhertz frequency regimes. Our results show that the orbits of binary MSPs could provide stringent constraints in microhertz range, thereby possibly complementing standard pulsar-timing-array analyses in the future.

authors.name: K. Liu, A. Chalumeau, H. Hu, S. Chen, L. Guillemot, J. Jang, M. Keith, J. Antoniadis, C. Bassa, A. Carleo, D. J. Champion, I. Cognard, G. H. Janssen, W. Jiang, R. Karuppusamy, E. F. Keane, M. Kramer, Y. Liu, M. B. Mickaliger, A. Parthasarathy, D. Perrodin, B. W. Stappers, G. Theureau, L. Wang

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
papers.summary: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to S\'ersic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($\mu_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The PHZ processing function for the physical properties of galaxies
papers.summary: Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NIR astrometric calibration
papers.summary: This paper presents the methodology and results of the astrometric calibration applied to the Euclid Near-Infrared (NIR) images in the Euclid Data Release 1, focusing on the techniques used to model and correct instrumental distortions, as well as the assessment of calibration quality. This work details the calibration pipeline, including quality control tests, and the evaluation of astrometric residuals against the Gaia DR3 catalogue and internal consistency metrics based on data encompassing more than one year of Euclid operation: the achieved accuracy is 30 mas for 97% of the total area, thus exceeding the requirements for Data Release 1. For the remaining 3%, accuracy declines due to a persistence correction issue: a method to correct the issue is presented. Furthermore, we discuss the stability of the solution over time, its dependence on source properties and instrument configuration, and outline the improvements planned for future Euclid data releases to enhance the astrometric calibration accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) - First NISP emission-line maps: Methodology, validation, and applications to galaxy evolution
papers.summary: We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$\alpha$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$\alpha$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$\alpha$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}\alpha}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): The MERge processing
papers.summary: The ESA satellite mission \Euclid was launched in July 2023 and started its regular observing mode in February 2024. The data from the \Euclid instruments Visible Camera (VIS) and the Near IR Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) are complemented by ground-based imaging data in the $u$, $g$ $r$, $i$, and $z$ bands to enable the determination of photometric redshifts and other galaxy properties. This paper describes the MERge processing function (MER PF) that has been developed and run for the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). The aim of the MER PF is to detect objects in the \Euclid imaging data, measure their properties, and combine them into a single multi-wavelength catalogue. In this paper we illustrate the design of the MER PF and introduce the different photometric methods applied to the data, which are Kron total flux, aperture photometry on Point Spread Functions (PSF) -matched images, template fitting photometry, and S\'ersic fitting photometry. We also present the various morphological measurements and quality flags that improve the scientific content of the output catalogues and better characterize the detected sources. We illustrate the processing and measurements that help to validate the MER PF results, which is an essential step to qualify the output for the public DR1 release. We discuss the global assessment of the photometric homogeneity and provide an internal comparison of our processing results. In addition, we give an extensive overview of the DR1 output data and the various processing scenarios

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
papers.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$\alpha$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)

papers.title: Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from the all-sky Wen & Han cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey
papers.summary: Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the clustering of galaxies and quasars now measure distances to precision of about one percent although galaxy clusters have so far given only marginal signals. We measure the BAO scale in the correlation function of \vNclus\ galaxy clusters with spectroscopic redshifts at $0.1<z<0.7$ from the Wen and Han (2024) all-sky catalog. After reconstruction of the density field, the BAO peak has a significance of $\vsigpost\sigma$ against a model without it, and gives $\DV/\rd=\vDVpost\pm\vDVpoststat\,({\rm stat})\pm\vDVpostsys\,({\rm sys})$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}=\vzeffv$, a \vfracposttot\% distance. We find that the statistical uncertainty is \vratiostat\ times smaller than that of the best earlier cluster measurement. The distance agrees with the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 within $\vnsdesipost\sigma$ and lies $\vnsplanckpost\sigma$ below Planck. We also measure the BAO scale in the \vTNgal\ galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey with a mean effective redshift (weighted by $n\,w^2$ with FKP weights), $z_{\rm eff}=\vTzeff$ For this all-sky galaxy sample we obtain $\aiso=\vTpreA^{+\vTpreAup}_{-\vTpreAlo}$ before reconstruction.

authors.name: Mart\'in G. Richarte, Diego G. Lambas

papers.title: Faster $\chi^2$ periodogram: Accelerating linear algebra with fast Toeplitz solvers
papers.summary: In recent years, the traditional Lomb--Scargle periodogram, relying on least-squares fitting of a sinusoid to data with a known mean, has been mostly superseded by its floating-mean extension---the generalized Lomb--Scargle periodogram---due to the superior robustness and accuracy of the latter. While further generalization to higher-degree trigonometric polynomials (known as the multiharmonic analysis of variance and the fast $\chi^2$ periodogram) has been known for decades, its usage remains relatively uncommon, mostly due to its significantly higher computational cost. Here we present a technique reducing the computational complexity of such an extension by combining a Toeplitz formulation of the system of normal equations with non-uniform fast Fourier transforms, coupled with condition-number monitoring to protect against numerical instability. When modified for practical efficiency rather than asymptotic computational complexity, our approach reaches speed-ups exceeding an order of magnitude over current state-of-the-art implementations across a wide range of hyperparameters when evaluated on multithreaded systems, while matching or exceeding their accuracy. Additionally, we provide a reference implementation used for benchmarking, along with the code used to generate the results presented in this work.

authors.name: Kacper Rutkowski, Rados{\l}aw Poleski

papers.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C-like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z = 1 to z = 0
papers.summary: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of \texttt{LEGA-C-like} galaxies in the \texttt{TNG100} simulation from $z=1$ to $z=0$ to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at $z=0$ as well as at $z=1$. Galaxies below $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim11.2$ have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of $\sim70\%$, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of $\sim60\%$. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to $z=0$ reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at $z=1$; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the \texttt{LEGA-C} epoch.

authors.name: Prem Kumar, Alina Boecker, Glenn van de Ven, Stefanie Reiter, Ling Zhu, Annalisa Pillepich, Prashin Jethwa, Sabine Thater

papers.title: The Impact of Seeding Threshold on Wandering Black Hole Populations and Merger Rates
papers.summary: Cosmological simulations following massive black holes (MBHs) with dynamical friction subgrid models predict hundreds to thousands of off-centre, wandering MBHs in massive galaxies. We investigate how the wandering MBH population changes with halo mass seeding threshold. We present cosmological zoom-in simulations of a $(15\,\mathrm{cMpc})^3$ volume to $z=2$, using the halo mass seeding thresholds of ASTRID, EAGLE and Illustris-TNG $(5\times10^{9}-5\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h)$, with a fixed MBH seed mass of $m_\mathrm{seed}=2\times10^{6}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. The subgrid dynamical friction model for MBHs switches to accurate integration around MBHs using the \textsc{ketju} module above $m_{\bullet} \geq 2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}/h$. We find that the seeding threshold greatly affects the MBH population: the number of seeded MBHs varies by a factor of ten and the number of wandering MBHs in the most massive galaxy ($M_\star=4.4\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) varies from 2 to 115. An MBH can become a wanderer in two ways. Interactions with other galaxies can offset a central MBH in low-mass galaxies ($M_\star\sim10^{8}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) if seeded in low mass halos $(\lesssim10^{10}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot/h)$. Alternatively, wandering MBHs can be added through mergers. The growth of the most massive MBHs is insensitive to the seeding threshold. While the total number of MBH mergers varies by an order of magnitude, the number of massive dynamically resolved MBH mergers differs by most a factor of $\sim3$ between seeding thresholds. The dynamically resolved binaries coalesce typically on timescales of $\sim10-250\,\mathrm{Myr}$ after becoming bound.

authors.name: Atte Keitaanranta, Peter H. Johansson, Alexander Rawlings, Antti Rantala, Thorsten Naab, Nianyi Chen, Max Mattero, Basti\'an Reinoso

papers.title: A Single-Shot Method for the Absolute Polarization Angle Calibration of CMB Telescopes with Artificial Sky Sources via Stellar Diffraction Encoding
papers.summary: Absolute polarization angle calibration of cosmic microwave background (CMB) telescopes at the $\lesssim 0.1^\circ$ level is needed to prevent instrumental mixing of $E$ modes into $B$ modes from biasing constraints on primordial gravitational waves and cosmic birefringence. Artificial polarized sky sources like drones, balloons, or satellites can provide calibration references, but transferring their emitted polarization angle from the payload frame to the celestial frame remains a challenge. We propose a calibrator architecture, applicable to any such source, in which a single dual-use grid-optic sets the polarization axis of the emitted millimeter-wave signal and also diffracts starlight into a co-aligned star camera. The resulting diffraction spectra record the grid's orientation relative to the stars, so that it can be measured directly on the sky without fine alignment between the camera and grid-optic. We describe the geometry and physics of this concept and show that it significantly simplifies obtaining the calibration angle the observatory needs, because precise payload attitude is no longer needed and the received polarization is insensitive to small line-of-sight errors. In simulations of 1000 real star fields that include camera-grid misalignment, lens distortion, lateral chromatic aberration, atmospheric refraction, and stellar colors, a single exposure recovers the polarizing grid-optic's orientation in the celestial frame with an uncertainty of $\simeq 0.002^\circ$, fifty times below the $0.1^\circ$ goal. We also discuss the hardware tolerances a physical calibrator must meet, which future work will test. Our results establish the feasibility of this approach and motivate development of a dual-use grid-optic.

authors.name: Dillon J. Bass, Bradley R. Johnson

papers.title: Posterior Predictive Checks for Gravitational-wave Populations: Limitations and Improvements
papers.summary: When selecting a model to characterize an astrophysical population, it is crucial to assess whether that model fits the data and, if not, how it can be improved. To this end, posterior predictive checks (PPCs) are a widely-used statistical test of model fit when inferring gravitational-wave source populations. However, PPCs exhibit limitations when assessing single-event parameters with large measurement uncertainty, like the spin tilt angles of the binary black holes (BBHs) observable with the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) detectors. When single-event inference is prior-dominated, traditional PPCs fail to flag even very poor model fits. In this work, we assess the efficacy of various alternative PPCs on poorly-constrained parameters. We compare PPCs conducted on event- vs. data-level parameters (e.g. posterior samples vs. maximum likelihood points), and explore two additional event-level PPCs: partial predictive checks and split predictive checks. Independent of measurement uncertainty, we find that PPCs on maximum likelihood parameters are always more discerning of model misspecification than any event-level PPC. However, when investigating simulated GWTC-3.0-like catalogs, none of the alternative PPCs show significant improvement over those traditionally used, indicating that at that sensitivity, any limited information in the data about spin tilts is insufficient to diagnose model misspecification. Finally, we apply our suite of PPCs to the spin magnitude and tilt distributions inferred in the most recent LVK catalog, GWTC-4.0. We conclude that the Gaussian Component Spins model used therein under-predicts BBHs with large spin magnitudes and over-predicts those with perfectly anti-aligned tilts.

authors.name: Simona J. Miller, Sophia Winney, Katerina Chatziioannou, Patrick M. Meyers

papers.title: Modifications of CMB Temperature and Polarization Quadrupole Signals in Thurston Spacetimes
papers.summary: Recent cosmological tests have discovered persistent CMB anomalies in the large-scale isotropy of the universe. Motivated thus by such anomalies that hint at potential departures from statistical isotropy present in recent cosmological observations with the advent of the 'precision cosmology' era, we are led to explore the viability of anisotropic Thurston geometries, described in William Thurston's geometrization conjecture. In this work, we examine the coherent temperature and polarization signals generated in the CMB sky by such geometries. We begin with introducing Thurston spacetimes as our background models and the formalism we use to obtain the patterns. We then construct a set of transfer equations relative to a given background and solve them for each spacetime geometry. We finally discuss the role of spatial curvature in these FLRW limiting models along with their underlying geometry, and attempt to establish some general results on the symmetries of the patterns produced by their time evolution in terms of temperature and Stokes parameters P, Q and U. We show the evolution of temperature and polarization amplitudes in terms of such Stokes parameters at different redshifts and attempt to isolate individual Thurston geometries.

authors.name: Tanay Gupta, Sukanta Panda, Rajib Saha

papers.title: Improving the resolution of double white dwarf systems with spaceborne gravitational wave observatories using a robust astrophysical prior
papers.summary: Resolving the crowded population of double white dwarf (DWD) binaries in data from spaceborne gravitational wave (GW) observatories (e.g., LISA, Taiji) remains a major analysis challenge. Comparable performance on addressing this problem has been achieved with two main approaches: global fit, in which resolvable sources are estimated simultaneously from the data, and iterative, where sources are estimated one at a time and subtracted out from the data. While the latter is computationally efficient, methods developed under this approach have traditionally followed a frequentist framework that ignores astrophysical priors. This work incorporates a strong astrophysical prior, derived from the mass limits of detached white dwarfs and linking the GW signal frequency $f$ with its time derivative $\dot{f}$, into the iterative \fitalgoname{} pipeline. Applied to simulated LISA and LISA-Taiji network data, the method increases the number of confidently resolved sources by ${\approx}7.3\%$ (LISA-only) and ${\approx}14.6\%$ (network) at matched detection rate, respectively, and improves parameter estimation accuracy.

authors.name: Shao-Dong Zhao, Xue-Hao Zhang, Soumya D. Mohanty, Yu-Xiao Liu

papers.title: Out-of-Equilibrium Effects in Non-Radial Relativistic Stellar Perturbations: A Model-Agnostic Formulation and Mode Analysis
papers.summary: We present a systematic, model-agnostic analysis of out-of-equilibrium effects, including viscosity and thermal conductivity, in non-radial oscillations of relativistic stars. Extending the Lindblom-Detweiler formalism, we construct, to our knowledge, the first general framework for linear, non-radial relativistic stellar perturbations that incorporates generic nonequilibrium corrections to the perfect-fluid sector in both the even- and odd-parity channels. Our framework is formulated in terms of the tensorial structure and thermodynamic decomposition of generic corrections without relying on any specific constitutive relations, thereby allowing us to elucidate, at a structural level, how these effects enter the perturbation equations and contribute to geometric deformations and fluid fluctuations. As an application, we consider the Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun fluid and perturbatively investigate shifts in the frequencies and damping times of modes connected to their perfect-fluid counterparts in the limit of vanishing transport coefficients. We also identify structural features of the closed eigenvalue problem that suggest the possibility of additional mode families. Our formalism provides a unified framework for analyzing how different relativistic fluid theories modify the structure of non-radial stellar perturbations.

authors.name: Takuya Katagiri, Victor Guedes, Kent Yagi

papers.title: From the Early Slope to Curvature: Future Prospects and challenges for Astrophysical Parameter Estimation Using the Core-Collapse Supernova High-Frequency Feature
papers.summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) signals from core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) contain both stochastic and deterministic components. Among these, the High-Frequency Feature (HFF), associated with Proto-Neutron Star (PNS) oscillations, has emerged as an observable for probing dense-matter physics. Previous studies of the HFF have primarily focused on its early-time slope as a diagnostic of PNS contraction and its dependence on the nuclear equation of state (EOS). In this work, we investigate recovering higher-order features of the HFF evolution, such as its curvature, from core-collapse supernova numerical simulations. By analyzing 2D and 3D waveforms injected into real interferometric noise, we apply the coherent WaveBurst algorithm in its cWB-XP implementation to reconstruct the HFF of recovered events. Comparing reconstructions at different signal strengths allows us to examine the extent to which the HFF remains accessible beyond its early linear evolution

authors.name: Alejandro Casallas-Lagos, Marek Szczepa\'nczyk, Michele Zanolin, Anthony Mezzacappa

papers.title: Hebbian self-organization of monosynaptic reflexes in a biologically realistic multiarticular limb
papers.summary: Spinal monosynaptic reflexes depend on patterns of connectivity between muscle spindle afferents and motoneurons that should reflect musculoskeletal dynamics. One possibility is that the details of these circuits are specified genetically, but this requires an unlikely coevolution of musculoskeletal and neural elements. Here we show how biomechanical structure can determine the connectivity of self-organized spinal circuits. Using a neuromechanical model combining a multi-joint limb, proprioceptive feedback, and Hebbian plasticity driven by motor babbling, we find that biologically realistic connectivity emerges spontaneously when babbling is neither too sparse nor too frequent. This results in strong homonymous projections, weaker heteronymous projections among functional synergists, and very weak connections among antagonists. This outcome also depends on musculoskeletal morphometry. Heteronymous synergies form when proximal muscles are strongest---the characteristic gradient of mammalian limbs--whereas excessively strong biarticular muscles lead to unphysiological antagonist coupling. The mechanisms differ: homonymous connections arise from direct sensorimotor correlation during fusimotor coactivation by beta motoneurons, while heteronymous connections depend on multi-joint dynamics that emerge only after homonymous reflexes stabilize and increasing muscle strength generates multisegmental motion. Overall, this study provides a mechanistic basis for fetal sensorimotor development and generates testable predictions about the consequences of naturally occurring and experimentally induced variations.

authors.name: Jonathan Realmuto, Erfan Nozari, Gerald E. Loeb

papers.title: A Dual-SOM Learner Model of Instructional Efficiency within Cognitive Load Theory
papers.summary: This paper presents a novel methodological framework, integrating a dual self-organising map (SOM) neural network architecture with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), for assessing instructional efficiency within learning environments. By representing curriculum content as a directed acyclic graph of topic dependencies, the proposed model captures collective learning behaviour across two core dimensions: academic performance and subjective/introspective mental effort. During SOM training, representative data sets of successful learner trajectories are compressed into two topologically ordered, identically structured neural networks: PSOM (performance space) and ESOM (mental effort space). By pairing these behavioural maps, the model serves as a decision-support tool that enables instructors to simultaneously pinpoint structural instructional design defects, such as hidden topic prerequisites, and evaluate collective cognitive load profiles. The implementation and performance of the PSOM component (and, by extension, its symmetrical twin, ESOM) is linked to an earlier modelling study employing a SOM with identical structure and encoding semantics situated in the same domain (i.e., a learning environment). This paper combines the study of behavioural phenomena with theoretical work on human cognitive architecture via SOM neurocomputational cognitive behavioural modelling.

authors.name: Spyridon Revithis

papers.title: The Shape of Individual Fitness Distributions and the Dynamics of Ecological Communities
papers.summary: Developing a mechanistic understanding of biogeography and biodiversity that predicts species abundances, distributions, and fluctuations is a central goal of community ecology. We develop a model, that can be seen as an extension of Hubbell's neutral theory, in which a focal species competes with the aggregate of all other species in a local community of fixed size. Each individual has its own competitive ability, and the shape of the distribution of these abilities is incorporated in the model, represented by distributions rather than single species-level values. Under complete mixing, symmetric competitive encounters without ties recover Hubbell's neutral model. We further incorporate immigration from a larger metacommunity and derive a diffusion approximation for the focal species' relative abundance. The model shows that competitive ability distributions with the same mean and variance can nevertheless yield different patterns of local abundance. Thus, species that appear equivalent when summarized by trait statistics need not be ecologically equivalent. Our framework links individual-level variability to population-level persistence and abundance and provides a way to examine how competition and immigration jointly shape ecological outcomes.

authors.name: Julie Rowlett, Leo Tingqvist

papers.title: Biases and Limits of AlphaFold Predictions for Non-Globular Proteins
papers.summary: AlphaFold has transformed protein structure prediction, making structural models accessible across the life sciences. We explore experimentally validated cases of non-globular proteins to uncover where predictions diverge from biologically relevant structural states and how molecular context shapes these discrepancies, guiding a more informed interpretation of AlphaFold models.

authors.name: Maria Cristina Aspromonte (University of Padova, Italy;), Alexander M. Monzon (University of Padova, Italy;), Miguel A. Andrade-Navarro (Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Germany;), Oriol B\'arcenas (Universitat Aut\`onoma de Barcelona and IQAC-CSIC, Spain;), Viktor Bartosik (Masaryk University, Czech Republic;), Pau Bernad\'o (Centre de Biologie Structurale, Montpellier, France;), Juan Cort\'es (LAAS-CNRS, Universit\'e de Toulouse, France;), Zsuzsanna Dosztanyi (Universit\'e de Montpellier, France;), Gabor Erdos (E\"otv\"os Lor\'and University, Hungary;), Isabella C. Felli (University of Florence, Italy;), Helena Gradi\v{s}ar (National Institute of Chemistry, Ljubljana, Slovenia;), San Had\v{z}i (University of Ljubljana, Slovenia;), Tam\'as Heged\H{u}s (Semmelweis University, Hungary;), Khalil Joron (Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel;), Pavel Kaderavek (Masaryk University, Czech Republic;), Eitan Lerner (Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel;), Dirk Linke (University of Oslo, Norway;), Pablo Mier (Universidad Pablo de Olavide, Spain;), Ana Panteli\'c (University of Belgrade and IMGGE, Serbia;), Roberta Pierattelli (University of Florence, Italy;), Salvador Ventura (Universitat Aut\`onoma de Barcelona and IQAC-CSIC, Spain;), Marija Vidovi\'c (University of Belgrade and IMGGE, Serbia;), Metaxia Vlassi (National Center for Scientific Research DEMOKRITOS, Greece), Lukas Zidek (Masaryk University, Czech Republic;), Silvio C. E. Tosatto (University of Padova, Italy;)

papers.title: A multilayer network-based modelling framework for epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus transmission in France
papers.summary: Epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus serotype 8 (EHDV-8) emerged in France in September 2023 but its transmission dynamics remain poorly characterised. We adapted a stochastic, spatially explicit compartmental model developed for bluetongue to reconstruct the 2023-24 EHDV-8 epidemic in cattle in mainland France. The model represented transmission across cantons, incorporating cattle demography, pasture cover, relative Culicoides abundance and temperature-dependent vector processes. Three networks represented between-canton spread through short-range vector dispersal (pasture network), non-commercial cattle movements between pastures of the same farm (farm network), and cattle trade (trade network). Using approximate Bayesian computation with sequential Monte Carlo (ABC-SMC), we calibrated the model to canton-week seroprevalence estimates derived from bulk-tank milk measurements. Calibration narrowed the plausible range of the baseline vector-mediated transmission parameter and favoured higher movement intensities through the farm network, although movement intensity remained uncertain. Simulation-based parameter recovery showed that calibration generally identified parameter regions capable of reproducing epidemic patterns comparable to the pseudo-observed data, although predictive performance varied among datasets and was typically lower than that obtained with the generating parameters. When applied to observed data, the calibrated model captured several features of the observed weekly median seroprevalence across sampled cantons, although discrepancies remained at some sampling times and predictive uncertainty was substantial. These results demonstrate how bulk-tank milk surveillance can inform the reconstruction of EHDV-8 epidemic patterns within a national-scale transmission framework. This framework provides a basis for future evaluation and optimisation of vaccination strategies.

authors.name: Viney Kumar, Ga\"el Beaun\'ee, Sandie Arnoux, Fabien Corbi\`ere, Beno\^it Durand, H\'el\`ene Cecilia

papers.title: Chemotactic aggregation as cue-mediated adaptation toward Nash equilibrium in a spatial patterning game
papers.summary: Chemotactic cells generate their own chemical gradients to form spatial patterns that support collective functions ranging from cooperative metabolism to immunity. Despite progress in understanding the optimality of chemotaxis in imposed chemical gradients, it remains unclear how close decentralized cell populations can come to maximizing the population-wide benefit of spatial organization through individual movement and local modulation of chemical gradients. We employ mean field game theory to characterize efficient spatial patterns achievable by decentralized populations as Nash equilibria: each agent optimizes its positioning given the spatial density of the other cells, whereas the population density is determined by the positioning of all individuals. We derive coupled dynamics of population movement and cue modulation that drive adaptation toward these equilibria and verify its structural correspondence to established phenomenological models of chemotactic pattern formation. We apply our framework to self-organized aggregation and numerically demonstrate that the dynamics can form multiple equilibrium patterns, some of which are comparable to the population-level optimum under moderate incentives to aggregate. We also show that the relative timescales of cue modulation and movement influence pattern selection and population-level efficiency: slower cue modulation can yield more coherent and efficient equilibrium patterns. Our framework thus highlights fundamental limits on collective optimization in decentralized cell populations, and suggests a functional role for timescales in self-organized coordination through environmental feedback.

authors.name: Masaki Kato, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi

papers.title: Inferring Neural Activity Changes under Recording Uncertainty with Transformers and Variational Inference
papers.summary: A difference in recorded firing rate across days may reflect a change in neuronal activity, missed spikes or recording a different neuron. We present a statistical approach that combines neuron tracking with Bayesian estimates of stationary mean recorded firing rates.
