papers.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,\mu\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop within $1\,\mu\text{s}$ while sustaining QPU-rate throughput. By introducing QuFrameISA, we cleanly decouple instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management. Execution is distributed across per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines (IREs) that resolve instructions against the frame via a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit enables independent, lock-free concurrent commits. To strictly guarantee the $1\,\mu\text{s}$ deadline, QuFrame pairs an asynchronous primary decoder with an on-chip fallback decoder that resolves in $144\,\text{ns}$, natively reconciling divergent updates in hardware without degrading logical error rates.

authors.name: Aleksandra \'Swierkowska, Ilgaz Er, Emmanouil Giortamis, Pramod Bhatotia

papers.title: Doppler effect on dual-downlink time-bin quantum key distribution and a proposed ephemeris-assisted witness-field correction
papers.summary: Time-bin entanglement is promising for satellite Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) due to its compatibility with telecom fiber networks, but its phase-sensitive measurements are vulnerable to Doppler effects induced by satellite motion. We present a spectral-temporal framework for time-bin-entangled photon pairs generated onboard a satellite via Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) and distributed to two Optical Ground Stations (OGSs) over independent downlinks with distinct Doppler shifts. Each OGS is equipped with an Unbalanced Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (UMZI) used to perform Bennett-Brassard-Mermin 1992 (BBM92) entangled-photon QKD. In a simulated Low Earth Orbit (LEO) pass with matched 400 ps analyzer delays, the received time-bin separation changes by at most 8.8 fs per link, while the combined carrier phase shifts by about 38 rad, which primarily degrades phase-basis correlations. After zero-Doppler calibration, this phase separates into independent signal-and idler-link contributions, allowing each station to correct its link Doppler phase shift locally, without real-time phase exchange between the stations. We propose an ephemeris-assisted feed-forward architecture, in which an auxiliary interferometer analyzes a co-propagating classical witness field to reconstruct the local Doppler-induced phase, which a phase modulator then compensates on the quantum channel. In a noise-free model, a 1 Hz sample-and-hold correction rate keeps the phase-basis Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) below 2% and retains 93% of the ideal asymptotic key yield. After 18 accumulated passes, the corrected finite secret key reaches 95% of its ideal length, whereas relabeling the parity from the ephemeris without optical correction reaches only about 8%.

authors.name: Sacha Gressani (FEMTO-ST, AUREA TECHNOLOGY, CSUG, UMLP), Luca Furfaro (FEMTO-ST, UMLP), Erik Kerstel (LAME-LIPhy, CSUG), Jean-Marc Merolla (FEMTO-ST)

papers.title: Long-distance continuous variable entanglement distribution over deployed fibre
papers.summary: Continuous-variable (CV) entanglement offers deterministic generation and room-temperature coherent detection for quantum networks, but distributing it over deployed fibre has been hindered by the need to stabilise optical phase, polarisation, and timing at remote receivers. Here we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first distribution of CV entanglement over deployed metropolitan fibre using independent coherent receivers. The two modes of a two-mode squeezed vacuum state are delivered to remote nodes through 23 km ($\approx 7$ dB loss) and 450 m ($\approx 1$ dB loss) deployed fibre links. Each node uses its own free-running laser and polarisation-diverse coherent receiver. Co-propagating pilot tones enable digital recovery of timing, phase and polarisation, while inter-mode correlations fix the quadrature alignment. We certify entanglement with a Simon-Duan value of $1.915\pm 0.013$, below the separability bound of 2 and a logarithmic negativity of $0.067\pm0.011$. By replacing optical stabilisation with digital reconstruction, our approach offers a practical route towards scalable CV quantum networks.

authors.name: Huy Q. Nguyen, Benjamin L. Larsen, Luiz C. C. P. Filho, Yijian Meng, Mikael {\O}. Lassen, Jonas S. Neergaard-Nielsen, Tobias Gehring, Ulrik L. Andersen, Adnan A. E. Hajomer

papers.title: Efficient simulation of variational quantum circuits: representation, accuracy and CPU/GPU allocation
papers.summary: Classical circuit simulation supports quantum software development and verification and provides a baseline for assessing quantum advantage. We compare gate-based statevector simulation, direct Pauli evolution and matrix product states for molecular and spin Variational Hamiltonian Ansatze and hardware-efficient ansatze on CPU/GPU systems, varying width, depth, precision and resource allocation. In the tested implementations, direct Pauli evolution benefits complex molecular VHA, whereas GPUs accelerate wider spin and hardware efficient circuits. Matrix product state is useful when limited entanglement permits accurate compression; corrected CPU FP32 can meet the tested tolerance while costing more than FP64. Workload size, startup, worker memory and task-specific profiling can change the preferred allocation. Matched NumPy Pauli updates accelerate two-layer full LiH by 3.45-fold; the GPU gives approximately 30-fold acceleration over 18-thread Aer for 28-qubit, four-layer TFIM, both in FP64. We provide a procedure for choosing representation, precision and worker allocation jointly, comparing the cost of complete energy evaluations under accuracy, memory and core constraints.

authors.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Radovan Re\v{c}ka, Ond\v{r}ej Knebl, Ivan Zelinka

papers.title: A unified approach to the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator via point transformations and Lie symmetries
papers.summary: We revisit the time-dependent harmonic oscillator (TDHO) in quantum mechanics based on the notion of equivalence transformations and Lie point symmetries. Within this framework, we give the most general point transformations depending on seven parameters which map from the TDHO to the usual harmonic oscillator (HO) and the other way around. As a byproduct we reconstruct the Schr\"odinger propagator (Mehler's kernel) for the time-independent harmonic oscillator. We demonstrate, without recourse to the Lewis--Riesenwert (LR) invariant, how Lie algebraic methods enable alternative derivation of the normalized wave functions of the TDHO by constructing solutions invariant under some specific subgroup of $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ combined with the gauge group. We further show that, on the relevant $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$-invariant solution family, the Lewis--Riesenfeld operator defines a compatible second-order differential constraint, thereby clarifying its relation to the Lie symmetry structure of the TDHO.

authors.name: F. G\"ung\"or, J. Negro

papers.title: Virtual Autopurification in Translationally Invariant Quantum States
papers.summary: We introduce virtual autopurification (VAP), a protocol for virtual purification that operates entirely within a single translationally invariant system. Virtual purification suppresses thermal fluctuations and decoherence noise by amplifying the dominant pure component of a mixed state, but its standard implementation requires multiple copies of the state and global entangled measurements. VAP avoids the multiple-copy overhead by constructing virtual copies from spatially separated subregions and performing entangled measurements only between them. Assuming clustering of correlations, we show that VAP reproduces the expectation values of the standard virtual purification protocol, with discrepancies that decay exponentially in both the buffer length and the inter-subregion distance. Numerical simulations support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate accurate implementation of virtual cooling with reduced resource requirements. Our results establish VAP as a resource-efficient and scalable approach to quantum-state purification in near-term devices.

authors.name: Atsushi Iwaki, Hideaki Hakoshima, Nobuyuki Yoshioka

papers.title: Linear-mode photon counting performance and intrinsic dark current in HgCdTe APDs for quantum optical applications
papers.summary: The performance of HgCdTe APDs for single photon detection at T=80 K has been characterized using a hybrized Resistive Trans-Impedance Amplifier (RTIA) and a deported Capacitance Trans-impedance amplifier (CTIA). The single-photon detection capacity was characterized with the HgCdTe APDs operated in linear mode with high APD gain, M>400, and hybridized with the RTIA. The measurements revealed an external photon detection efficiency (PDE) of 42 % to 55 %, and a dark count rate (DCR) of 2.6 MHz to 17 MHz, for an amplitude threshold ranging from 2.5 to 4.5 times the rms noise of the amplifier. Taking into account the unity gain quantum efficiency, QE=63%, this corresponds to an internal PDE ranging from 66 % to 86 %. Using the deported CTIA, it was demonstrated that the high level of DCR is not the intrinsic limit of the APD technology. The CTIA approach enables direct measurement of the APD dark current, Idark, with gain-normalized dark current levels as low as Idark/M=10.9 fA at M = 450. This corresponds to a DCR of 150 Hz which is compatible with the requirements for most of the quantum photonics applications.

authors.name: Arthur Charrier (CEMHTI), Timoth{\'e}e Guerra (CEMHTI), Nicolas Baier (CEA-LETI), Julie Abergel (CEA-LETI), Antoine Coquiard (CEA-LETI), Amaury Mavel (INL - S\&N, INL - H\&N), Sebastien Renet (CEA), Frederic Berger (UR EMGR), Aur{\'e}lie Vandeneynde (CEA-LETI), Sandy Brunet-Manquat (CEA-LETI), Jean-Alain Nicolas (CEA-LETI), Jean-Luc Moro (FEMTO-ST, CNRS, UMLP), Jean-Marc Merolla (FEMTO-ST, CNRS, UMLP), Johan Rothman

papers.title: Bound entanglement as a trigonometric moment problem
papers.summary: Entangled states that are positive under partial transposition (PPT) are the main obstruction to a simple description of entanglement. We study three basic questions about them within a class of multiqubit states, the mixtures, with real but possibly negative weights, of products of equatorial spin coherent states of several groups of qubits: which PPT entangled states belong to the class, how robust their entanglement is to white noise, and how small their rank can be. In this class each question becomes a question about a truncated trigonometric moment problem. Every such state is PPT across every bipartition, and it is fully separable exactly when an associated multi-level Toeplitz matrix is the moment matrix of a positive measure on the torus. We answer the three questions exactly in the following cases. For three qubits, every rank-four PPT entangled state with nonzero Lorentz invariant belongs to the class after invertible local operators, which proves a working hypothesis of Garberg, Irgens and Myrheim and yields a complete set of invariants for this seven-dimensional family; among the states with vanishing invariant, exactly a one-parameter family belongs to it. For every three-qubit state built from an unextendible product basis, the white-noise threshold for full separability is $\lambda^*=1-2/(1+\sqrt{1+s})$ with a local-unitary invariant $s\in(0,1]$, and $\lambda^*=3-2\sqrt2$ for the Shifts basis; a witness in closed form detects every entangled state of this family with eight local Pauli settings. For two groups of qubits we construct extremal states of minimal rank, and for three groups we determine the minimal rank of entanglement within the class in several configurations.

authors.name: Lilong Qian, Teng Zhang

papers.title: From BBM92 Measurements to Secure Keys: Challenges in a Practical Implementation
papers.summary: The protocol introduced by C. H. Bennett, G. Brassard and N. D. Mermin in 1992 (BBM92) is one of the most important and widely adopted quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. As with any other QKD protocol, its practical security depends on satisfying the assumptions underlying its theoretical security proofs. Here, we examine two common implementations of BBM92: a conventional passive receiver and a time-multiplexed configuration that halves the number of detectors. We characterise the passive polarisation analysers common to both architectures and present experimental results obtained with the time-multiplexed receiver, employing a continuous-wave (CW) pumped spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) source of polarisation-entangled photon pairs and threshold detectors. We investigate the challenges encountered during post-processing when attempting to satisfy the requirements of existing security proofs and discuss the gap between theoretical security assumptions and the extraction of a provably secure cryptographic key.

authors.name: Karolina P. Schatz, Elia Falcioni, Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Marco Lucamarini

papers.title: Sharp rank thresholds and cubic support in PPT extensions of completely symmetric states
papers.summary: For completely symmetric states on $d\ge3$ parties of actual local rank $N\ge3$, the least rank of an entangled state passing any prescribed finite positive level of the PPT extension hierarchy is $3d+N-3$. At equality, the two- and three-party marginals recover a ternary plane cubic shared by every extension. On this cubic the hierarchy becomes exact at a finite level precisely when every singularity outside the zero locus of the contraction quadratic is a split real node. We give the first exact level or an exact feasibility test for it, independent of $d$. On a smooth cubic the thresholds along the specified paths to the square of a flex tangent reduce to elliptic division and have unique rank-two Gram matrices. On reflection-invariant paths we obtain a quartic formula and the leading asymptotic constant. The least rank for entanglement itself is $3d+N-5$, and we classify equality. An explicit rational rank-nine three-qutrit state on a smooth cubic passes the first extension level and fails the second.

authors.name: Qian Lilong, Teng Zhang

papers.title: A Relativistic Quantum Mechanical Formulation of Wu-Shaknov Entanglements
papers.summary: It is suggested that a spontaneous formation of quantum mechanical entanglements does actually occur between spin, helicity and polarization states involved in creation-annihilation processes. A framework built up earlier that presumably affords a unified relativistic quantum mechanical description of free particle-antiparticle pairs of any spin is used to propose a comprehensive formulation of Wu-Shaknov entanglements. Explicit relationships between amplitudes and Born-like probabilities associated to incoming and outgoing states are obtained thereafter on the basis of certain theoretical assumptions. The behaviours of these relationships under the action of a dynamical group which is taken to supply observational correlations for different frames in spacetime are then specified. It appears that a modified version of some of the conventional conservation laws may afford a set of general selection rules for the formation of relativistic entanglements.

authors.name: J. G. Cardoso

papers.title: On a local hidden-variable model for postselected EPR correlations
papers.summary: A theoretical and numerical analysis of a Bell-type experiment is presented, where linear polarization measurements on nonmaximally entangled two-qubit states are modeled through a sigmoid-based threshold mechanism that violates the fair-sampling assumption required by the CHSH inequality. Numerical simulations characterize how closely this local construction can reproduce quantum-like correlations in the postselected detected sample, for both the |Phi_r> and |Psi_r> states over a range of entanglement parameters. For the tested configurations, the model produces CHSH-type violations only in the postselected detected sample through a setting-dependent detection mechanism, operating outside the assumptions of both the CHSH inequality and Mermin's 82.8% efficiency bound. The model is not in conflict with loophole-free Bell experiments, which specifically close the detection loophole exploited here. The CH--Eberhard analysis in the one-detector-per-side configuration yields J < 0 throughout the full range of entanglement parameters, as required for a strictly local model. The model is further extended with a local adaptive-threshold mechanism implementing one-sided memory. A paired comparison shows that this specific memory rule produces a systematic and reproducible shift in the CH--Eberhard parameter J relative to the fixed-threshold model, while leaving the CH--Eberhard analysis qualitatively unchanged under the tested conditions. The results characterize how a local, setting-dependent postselection mechanism shapes Bell-test statistics across a range of entanglement parameters, within the specific configurations and threshold rules tested.

authors.name: Daniele Cenni

papers.title: No-Go Theorems for Ordered Universal Entanglement Purification
papers.summary: Entanglement purification is a fundamental tool for obtaining high-fidelity entangled states used in various quantum technologies. It aims to increase the fidelity of noisy shared entangled states with a fixed maximally entangled state through LOCC. In distributed quantum systems, such as networks employing quantum repeaters, limited memory, probabilistic entanglement generation, and unequal storage times can leave a finite collection of nonidentical pairs. Their states may remain incompletely characterized even when calibrated preparation and storage records establish their fidelity ordering. Recent work has investigated whether fidelity ordering permits nontrivial universal purification. A nontrivial universal $n$-to-1 protocol must, conditioned on success, never lower the highest input fidelity and strictly increase it for at least one allowed joint input. Although no-go results have been established for a restricted class of LOCC protocols, the corresponding question for general LOCC has remained unresolved. Here, we study ordered universal purification under separable operations. Specifically, for every fixed finite $n\ge2$, we prove that when independently prepared two-qubit pairs range over the full family of states above a fixed fidelity threshold $0\le F_*<1$, any separable success map that never lowers the highest input fidelity on the allowed ordered inputs must preserve that fidelity exactly whenever it succeeds. This excludes nontrivial universal LOCC purification even for arbitrarily high input fidelities, without imposing a positive lower bound on success probability. ...

authors.name: C. L. Liu

papers.title: Measurement-order dependence bounds uncertainty, contextuality, steering, and Bell nonlocality
papers.summary: Two quantum measurements applied to the same input in opposite orders give two joint distributions of the same outcomes. For L\"uders instruments we measure how far apart these order records can be, over all inputs, by their total-variation distance $\mathcal{T}$, their Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathcal{J}$ (in bits), and their squared Hellinger distance. These order scores vanish exactly when the measurements commute, and $\mathcal{T}=\|[A,B]\|/4$ for two binary sharp observables. Some pairs of bases exceed mutually unbiased bases in squared Hellinger score, and in odd dimensions in $\mathcal{J}$, although their minimal entropy sum is smaller. For projective measurements, a Maassen-Uffink bound $q>0$ implies $\mathcal{T}\ge1-2^{-q}$ and a positive lower bound on $\mathcal{J}$. Measuring all observables of a scenario in sequence defines a joint distribution, so violations of noncontextuality, steering, and Bell inequalities are bounded by distances between order records. For correlation Bell inequalities with binary sharp observables, the squared Bell operator is a symmetrized (Jordan) part minus tensor products of local commutators. If one party has two settings, the violation is bounded bilinearly in the two parties' order scores; we conjecture this bound in general. On Clifford realizations it would follow from a Hilbert-Schmidt variant of Grothendieck's inequality, which we prove when one party has at most three settings. For three binary sharp measurements, the violation of Bell's original inequality by a maximally entangled state equals an order effect in three-measurement records of the maximally mixed state minus four times an alternation probability. For the rank-one Klyachko-Can-Binicio\u{g}lu-Shumovsky pentagon on a qutrit, the violation is at most the largest product of the order scores of two crossing diagonals, with equality at the maximal violation.

authors.name: Shengjun Wu

papers.title: Number-correlated photon entanglement with a quantum memory interferometer
papers.summary: Strong photon-photon interactions are central to quantum optical technologies yet remain challenging to realise at the single-photon level. Here, we show how embedding a quantum memory within a Mach-Zehnder interferometer enables a coherent transformation that converts single-mode photon states into number-correlated entangled states. Using an off-resonant ladder-type atomic interaction, storage and retrieval within a quantum memory maps a single-photon excitation onto a pair of photons across distinct optical modes via a driving control field. Embedding this within an interferometer deterministically produces an effective transformation in the photon number basis: $\sum_n a_n |n\rangle \to \sum_n a_n |n\rangle |n\rangle$ without relying on conventional optical nonlinearities. Measurement of one mode enables photonic non-demolition detection, state preparation, and frequency conversion as applications of the same underlying transformation. These results establish quantum memories embedded within an interferometric architecture as a platform for measurement-induced photon-photon interactions and the generation of Gaussian and non-Gaussian entangled states.

authors.name: Imogen Forbes, Vincent Boyer, Louis Edwards-Pratt, Mahirul Khan, Sougato Bose, Thomas M Hird

papers.title: On Reaction Depth and Fast Fault-Tolerant Boolean Logic
papers.summary: Reducing runtimes of quantum applications is critical for practical viability. On quantum computers, the runtime can depend both on the speed of quantum operations and on how often the program must wait for the classical coprocessor to determine adaptive operations. Some recent approaches to reducing this overhead have focused on minimizing the "reaction depth" of a computation, informally defined as the number of times the classical coprocessor must be consulted while running a quantum program. In this work, we formalize the notion of reaction depth. We find several subtleties in this theory. For example, we distinguish the reaction depth of a circuit from that of a circuit run, and show that the magic depth of a unitary can be higher than the reaction depth once compiled into Clifford computation and magic state injection. We then focus on the specific case of coherent Boolean logic, a common and expensive component in quantum algorithms. We use a natural gateset for fast operations with Low-Density Parity Check (LDPC) codes, which consists of homogeneous $Z$- and $X$-type Pauli Product Measurements (PPMs), alongside a supply of Toffoli states. We prove that, using this gateset, any Boolean arithmetic circuit can be implemented on a quantum computer with constant quantum depth and constant reaction depth, at the cost of exponential space and leaving some qubits "dirty". Using the same gateset we find two efficient AutoAND circuits that require only a Toffoli state and homogeneous PPMs. We then give efficient implementations of the quantum ripple-carry adder and quantum schoolbook multiplier, which require a low number of heterogeneous PPMs for uncomputation. We find implementations competitive with the state-of-the-art despite the restricted gateset.

authors.name: Christopher Kang, Alexander Cowtan, Adam Bene Watts, Guillaume Dauphinais, Benjamin Ide

papers.title: Coherent-Response and Thermal-Fluctuation Information in Cavity-Magnon Magnetometry
papers.summary: Magnetic sensing with cavity--magnon systems typically relies on the coherent response, while field-dependent fluctuations are treated as measurement noise. Here, we show that the variance of a measured microwave quadrature provides a distinct source of magnetic-field information. For repeated phase-sensitive measurements of a calibrated quadrature, we derive the Gaussian likelihood and show that its Fisher information separates exactly into two terms. The coherent-displacement term depends on the field derivative of the quadrature mean, and the thermal-fluctuation term depends on the field derivative of its variance. Both terms are accessible from the same measurement record, but their optimal operating conditions differ. For the amplitude quadrature, the dimensionless coherent response factor reaches its global maximum at cooperativity $C=2$, corresponding to a coupling strength $g=\sqrt{2\kappa_a\kappa_m}$, and at linewidth-normalized detunings $\delta_a=\delta_m=\pm 1$. In the near-resonance approximation, the reduced variance-information term is globally maximized at cavity--magnon frequency matching, $\Delta_a=\Delta_m$, and approaches a finite limit at large cooperativity. We map the relative contributions of the two terms across drive frequencies, drive strengths, and temperatures. Strong coherent driving favors displacement-based sensing, whereas at finite temperature the variance contribution can dominate under weak driving and remain finite even when the coherent-displacement contribution vanishes. These results establish a measurement-specific framework for cavity--magnon magnetometry and identify operating regimes for exploiting the quadrature mean, its variance, or both.

authors.name: G. Zhao, X. -F. Qian

papers.title: The magical memory cost of entanglement spectrum compression
papers.summary: How much quantum memory is needed to faithfully retain the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after separating out Bell pairs through local unitaries? We derive the exact tradeoff between Bell-pair yield, residual memory, and reconstruction fidelity under local unitaries, defining an operational measure of entanglement-spectrum complexity. Smoothed entanglement spread bounds this memory cost from below, while diverging nonlocal magic forces unbounded memory at any fixed positive fidelity. Chaotic circuit dynamics exhibit a transient memory peak whose height increases with system size, followed by declining cost despite continued entropy growth. A large typical Haar-random state requires only an accuracy-dependent memory, whereas stationary fermionic Gaussian states retain a growing cost with size. In the circuits studied, the multiscale spectral structure associated with entanglement catalysis also has a practical consequence for matrix product state compression, yielding a multiplicative overhead not captured by the conventional entropy-based bond dimension estimate.

authors.name: Matias Karjula, Vilma Nieminen, Teemu Ojanen, Tapio Ala-Nissila, Moein N. Ivaki

papers.title: Environment-assisted imaginary time evolution in feedback-based quantum algorithms
papers.summary: The Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON) prepares ground states without classical parameter optimization, but requires deep circuits and can stagnate away from the ground state as a consequence of barren plateaus and symmetry protection. In order to avoid stagnation, imaginary time evolution (ITE) layers can be incorporated into FALQON layers, enhancing FALQON convergence. However, applying a non-unitary ITE layer in a closed quantum system is not possible, and approximations must be made to use ITE on real hardware; using an open quantum system formulation to incorporate ITE into FALQON represents a better approach. We describe ITE as a quantum operation induced by an environment, and combine it with the FALQON feedback law. In simulations of a frustrated Ising chain (ANNNI) and of MaxCut, the resulting algorithm prepares the ground state starting from any initial state, where FALQON can fail, and needs fewer layers on average when the initial state is fixed for the two investigated problems. The CITE-FALQON advantage strongly depends on the system phase for the ANNNI chain, and on the graph weights for the MaxCut problem.

authors.name: J. C. Bellizotti Souza, M. C. de Oliveira

papers.title: The limits of magic-state cultivation
papers.summary: Fault tolerance is understood through Pauli algebra, which fails at non-Clifford gates. Circuits such as magic-state cultivation, which checks an encoded T state with physical T gates, have therefore lacked an exact theory of which faults are harmful. We develop such a theory and show that, for any circuit that prepares a magic state with non-Clifford gates and postselection, one stabilizer code on the non-Clifford gates decides which faults are harmful. This ties cultivation to distillation, bounds its T-count from below and gives an exact test. For a single check on an ideally encoded state, the fault distance reduces to Pauli algebra on the code. As a use case, we analyze the S gates that have stood in for T gates in the design of cultivation. We show that this proxy can only overstate the fault distance of such a check, and that the checks in use, on color and surface codes, tolerate at most half as many faults as their code allows. The theory also yields nearest-neighbor checks that keep the full distance, certified up to code distance nine.

authors.name: Lloren\c{c} Balada Gaggioli, Jakub Mare\v{c}ek

papers.title: Hurst Exponent Estimation with Quantum Wavelets
papers.summary: How accurately can the Hurst exponent $H$ of fractional Brownian motion be estimated from repeated preparations of a single amplitude-encoded path, when every measurement interrogates the same realization? We extend the $\epsilon$-decimated quantum nondecimated wavelet transform in three directions: we remove the endpoint jump of circular filtering, derive the sampling distribution of the estimator, and compare readouts at equal query budgets. A one-qubit mirror extension removes the jump and keeps every coefficient that straddles a fold of the same order as an interior coefficient, for any compactly supported filter and circular shift. The transform for any such filter is compiled from the paraunitary lattice of its filter bank, and the energy share of a level is the success probability of one multiply-controlled reflection, which is both the controlled unitary of a Hadamard test and the oracle of amplitude estimation. For filters with at least two vanishing moments we prove a root-$N$ central limit theorem for the log-energy contrasts, independent of the limiting path norm, so the studentized estimator is asymptotically standard normal for deterministic query budgets under which the success count at every level diverges. For sparse counts we give a working multinomial--lognormal likelihood, exact in its readout model for direct measurement, and check its coverage by simulation. For paths of length $512$, mirroring reduces RMSE by a factor of $3$--$10$ for $H\ge0.5$, and with exact shares the nondecimated db2 estimator is $6$--$14\%$ above the root Cram\'er--Rao bound. Hadamard level tests are less accurate than direct measurement of the leading qubits at every budget. At $H=0.9$ and $2^{20}$ queries, maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation attains RMSE $0.0347$, against $0.0451$ for direct measurement and $0.0295$ with exact shares.

authors.name: Brani Vidakovic

papers.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
papers.summary: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures. We present CREST, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that evaluates circuit-region compatibility before routing. It encodes gate dependencies and logical-qubit interactions alongside each candidate region's connectivity and current calibration attributes; bidirectional cross-graph attention relates the two representations, while real-device execution outcomes supervise candidate ranking. The trained scorer is reused with updated calibration attributes. Evaluations on 324 circuits from seven datasets on TianYan-176 show that CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the strongest baseline and achieves the highest mean fidelity on every dataset. Furthermore, using updated calibration attributes, the same trained model maintains the highest overall mean fidelity across six measurement dates without retraining. With a unified model of circuit-region compatibility, CREST improves execution fidelity across diverse workloads and sustains that advantage as hardware calibration changes.

authors.name: Wenjie Sun, Xiaoyu Li, Zhigang Wang, Yuchen He, Shengbin Wang, Hantao Sun

papers.title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.summary: Symmetry-preserving (SP) variational quantum circuits restrict evolution to physically relevant sectors of Hilbert space, but symmetry preservation alone does not guarantee accessibility within those sectors. We show that a restricted generator set can possess a residual dynamical Lie algebra whose commutant further decomposes the target symmetry sector into invariant blocks. The associated block populations are conserved and impose a kinematic upper bound on the fidelity with a target state. We then invert this diagnostic into a circuit-design principle: candidate SP generators can be screened before variational optimization by asking whether they break the residual commutant, which invariant blocks they couple, and what adjoint module they generate under the residual algebra. For two orthogonal residual blocks we prove that a single elementary real inter-block rotation generates the full orthogonal algebra. We further derive a complex escape criterion: if the real and imaginary parts of an inter-block seed are independent over the residual intertwiner algebra, the generated module is the full complex coupling space and the enlarged algebra becomes special unitary. A connected residual-block graph yields a natural multi-block generalization and suggests minimum-cost spanning-tree circuit design. We demonstrate this design principle in the XXZ and Hubbard models, where residual-algebra screening identifies SP circuit extensions that remove the relevant accessibility obstructions. These examples establish a unified route from residual-symmetry diagnosis and fidelity bounds to predictive quantum circuit design.

authors.name: Sahinur Reja

papers.title: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using a Multilayer Ion Trap Chip with an Integrated Radio Frequency Resonator
papers.summary: We present the experimental preparation of a radio frequency (RF)-dressed-state qubit, the coherent operation of a single RF-dressed qubit, and the selective readout of RF-dressed hyperfine states of $^{171}$Yb${^+}$ ions trapped using a novel microstructured ion trap chip. We demonstrate the individual addressing of RF-dressed-state qubits in a two-ion Coulomb crystal. To this end, we developed, manufactured, and characterized a trap chip specifcally designed for quantum information processing with RF-dressed-state qubits. The chip consists of multiple layers, one of which includes an integrated resonator that creates a gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude along the axis of a linear ion crystal. This RF gradient enables the individual addressing of dressed qubit states as well as their coupling. We characterize the ion trap chip experimentally using the hyperfine states of the electronic ground state of laser cooled $^{171}$Yb${^+}$ ions and by applying a single, global, modulated RF field oscillating near 12.6 GHz that drives dressed-state resonances. We present a microfabricated multilayer ion trap chip specifically designed for quantum information processing based on dressed-state qubits. This ion trap chip consists of multiple layers, one of which includes an integrated radio frequency (RF) resonator, creating a gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude that allows for individual qubit addressing and qubit-qubit coupling. We experimentally characterize this ion trap chip demonstrating dressed-qubit state preparation, coherent single dressed-qubit operation, and dressed-state-selective read-out using hyperfine states of the electronic ground state of $^{171}$Yb${^+}$. For this purpose, a global modulated RF driving field oscillating near 12.6 GHz is applied to the ions. In addition, we demonstrate individual addressing of dressed-state qubits in a two-ion Coulomb crystal.

authors.name: Ivan A. Boldin, Elham Esteki, Bogdan Okhrimenko, Friederike Giebel, Konstantin Thronberens, Amado Bautista-Salvador, Christian Ospelkaus, Christof Wunderlich

papers.title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
papers.summary: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling. Here we construct a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance. Under suitable conditions, we prove a time-uniform $O(\lambda^2)$ bound on the difference between the predicted and exact reduced density matrices, where $\lambda$ is the system-bath coupling strength. Our construction completes the Redfield generator by imposing detailed balance while matching its dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance. In this approach, TR-KMS detailed balance is compatible with resonance matching, whereas its counterpart without time reversal is not. In a benchmark against the exact microscopic dynamics of two coupled oscillators, our equation maintains $O(\lambda^2)$ accuracy across secular and nonsecular regimes, outperforming the existing detailed-balance equations tested. These results provide a systematic route from microscopic models to thermodynamically consistent descriptions of open quantum dynamics beyond the secular approximation.

authors.name: Ji-Hui Pei, Jin-Fu Chen

papers.title: Comment on "The eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the toroidal dipole operator'
papers.summary: We show here that the spectrum of the operator $\hat{T}_3^{(\theta)}$ studied by Anghel and Dolineanu (Phys. Scr. {\bf 98} (2023) 015223) is continuous, not discrete, contrary to what is claimed by the authors of the paper to which this comment refers. Consequently, there is no splitting of the energy levels corresponding to this operator that could be observed experimentally.

authors.name: G. Vaman

papers.title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders
papers.summary: We study extreme-value phenomena for random samples in partially ordered sets through their meets and joins, the order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. In this paper we consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. We analyse these extrema both at fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, identifying almost-sure collapse to the bottom or top elements and critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.

authors.name: Elia Bisi, Fabio Deelan Cunden, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligab\`o

papers.title: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control
papers.summary: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-site energies and following a fixed interval of integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels. An exact Bloch-determinant identity links the physical transfer discriminant to the bands of a periodic reference operator. For the golden cell frequency, we prove that, on a common full-measure set of phases and for every finite value of the spacer control, the physical spectrum in the open reference bands is critical, with purely singular-continuous spectrum and zero Lyapunov exponent, while the spectrum strictly outside the bands is pure point, with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions. Validated IDS bounds certify repeated critical--localized alternation of the same fixed spectral fraction at successive spacer controls. Spacer shifts move the physical levels and reference-band edges at different rates, allowing us to reshape finite-chain return windows and place their endpoints at prescribed controls. An affine recalibration relocates the control family exactly.

authors.name: Xin Wang, Pei-Jie Chang, Dong Ruan, Gui-Lu Long

papers.title: The $S$ and Double-Exponential Transformations with a Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals
papers.summary: Three-centre two-electron Coulomb and hybrid integrals over exponential-type functions involve semi-infinite radial integrals containing oscillatory spherical Bessel functions. We investigate the combination of the $S$ transformation with Fourier-type double-exponential (DE) quadrature for their accurate and efficient numerical evaluation. The $S$ transformation transfers derivatives from the spherical-Bessel factor to the radial amplitude, converting the integral into a sine representation particularly well suited to Fourier-type DE quadrature. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the combined $S+\mathrm{DE}$ approach can substantially reduce the number of quadrature nodes required to achieve high accuracy compared with direct DE. We further identify a geometry-dependent oscillation-to-damping ratio and establish a convergent moment expansion in the weakly oscillatory regime. Exploiting this complementary representation markedly enhances the numerical reliability of the algorithm in regimes where direct oscillatory quadrature becomes inefficient. The method is examined through semi-infinite radial integrals and complete H$_2$O and C$_2$H$_4$ molecular integrals over Slater-type functions, with comparisons against complete $S$-series evaluations and values reported in the literature.

authors.name: Hassan Safouhi

papers.title: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory?
papers.summary: We develop a model, that we call local semiclassical gravity, based on the distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations (EFEs) sourced by the local quantum state, i.e. the reduced density matrix of the local system updated by collapses (only) in its past light cone. We propose this as the basis of a relativistically causal generally covariant gravitisation of relativistic quantum theory in $1+3$ spacetime dimensions. We derive the weak-field limit which exhibits the explicitly causal dynamical structure of the theory, and recover the Schr\"odinger-Newton (SN) system in the nonrelativistic limit. This proposal can thus be understood as a causal completion of the SN equation, a nonlinear extension to quantum theory. We analyze relativistic quantum measurements in this nonlinear setup, showing that these do not lead to superluminal signalling if quantum states update (only) in the future light-cone of the measurement region. We give explicit examples of quantum measurements on a spatial superposition and on entangled subsystems showing how, in the weak field limit, discontinuities in the expectation value of the stress-energy tensor can be consistent with distributional solutions to the (linearised) semiclassical EFEs. We also highlight that the theory allows non-standard measurements via its nonlinearities. These effective ``readout devices'' can approximately determine a quantum state without affecting it through the state's influence on the classical gravitational field and hence can implement approximate quantum state cloning. Nonetheless, the theory does not allow superluminal signalling, although it does violate the quantum no-signalling principle. We further show that the classical gravitational field is generally not locally causal in the sense of Bell. We present several paths to test the model against low-energy quantum gravity in tabletop experiments.

authors.name: Samuel Fedida, Adrian Kent

papers.title: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains
papers.summary: We investigate the spontaneous emission of a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By tuning the chain from a metallic to a semiconducting character through dimerization, we analyze how the electronic structure of an atomic-scale scatterer, together with the illumination profile, determines the strength, bandwidth, and spatial structure of the spontaneous emission enhancement. The resonant enhancement depends on both spectral matching and the emitter position relative to the induced charge and field patterns. In metallic chains, the nearly harmonic energy spectrum leads to overlapping optical transitions and strong resonances. For semiconducting chains, dimerization opens a gap and leads to a modified density of electronic states, redistributing the response over a broader spectral range and reducing its peak intensity. Coulomb interactions affect the optical resonances through blueshift or modification of their spatial character, and act differently on collective and single-particle-like excitations. Finally, we show that the same mechanisms demonstrated in atomic chains persist in realistic quasi-one-dimensional systems, including trans-polyacetylene chains and graphene nanoribbons. Our findings indicate a general direction for engineering light-matter interactions at the atomic scale, and may offer design principles for tunable nanoscale photonic and quantum-optical devices.

authors.name: Abhishek Ghosh, David Dams, Antton Babaze, Garnett Bryant, Carsten Rockstuhl, Andr\'es Ayuela, Karolina S{\l}owik, Marta Pelc

papers.title: A Bose-Hubbard quantum thermal machine
papers.summary: This work proposes a quantum thermal machine comprised of interacting ultracold bosons confined in a one-dimensional optical lattice and modeled by the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. We consider an Otto-inspired cycle with strokes that change the interaction strength between bosons, in addition to standard thermalization and compression/expansion strokes. We find that these interaction changes can be manipulated to enhance the performance of the thermal machine, outperforming non-interacting cycles. In particular, when operating as a heat engine, the cycle can achieve its largest work output and near-Carnot efficiency by compressing the medium at strong repulsion into a Mott insulator state. Additionally, we find that decreasing interactions after the compression stroke favors and enhances the engine operation, whereas increasing interactions favors refrigeration cycles. The findings of this work further show that controlling the interactions across quantum phases of matter can be harnessed as a useful thermodynamic resource.

authors.name: Felipe Isaule, Juan E. Bernate, Francisco J. Pe\~na, Patricio Vargas, Thom\'as Fogarty

papers.title: On the Role of Quantum Communication and Loss in Attacks on Quantum Position Verification
papers.summary: We study the role of quantum communication in attacks on quantum position verification. In this work, we construct the first known example of a QPV protocol that is provably secure against unentangled attackers restricted to classical communication, but can be perfectly attacked by local operations and a single round of simultaneous quantum communication, indicating that allowing for quantum communication during the execution of the protocol may break security in a different way than just by establishing shared entanglement. We also show that any QPV protocol with a positive security gap against classical communication can be transformed into a protocol with an explicit positive gap between the honest prover's success probability and that of initially unentangled attackers using a single round of simultaneous quantum communication. We further show, using arguments based on the monogamy of entanglement, that the task of Bell state discrimination cannot be done locally with a single round of quantum communication, not even probabilistically (when we allow attackers to say loss sometimes), making this the first fully loss-tolerant QPV task secure against quantum communication attacks. Finally, we observe that any multi-round QPV protocol can be attacked with a linear amount of entanglement if the loss is high enough.

authors.name: Rene Allerstorfer, Harry Buhrman, Florian Speelman, Philip Verduyn Lunel

papers.title: Local entanglement of electrons in 1D hydrogen molecule
papers.summary: The quantum entanglement entropy of the electrons in one-dimensional hydrogen molecule is quantified locally using an appropriate partitioning of the two-dimensional configuration space. Both the global and the local entanglement entropy exhibit a monotonic increase when increasing the inter-nuclear distance, while the local entropy remains peaked at the middle between the nuclei with its width decreasing. Our findings show that at the inter-nuclear distance where stable hydrogen molecule is formed, the quantum entropy shows no peculiarity thus indicating that the entropy and the energy measures display different sensitivity with respect to the interaction between the two identical electrons involved. One possible explanation is that the calculation of the quantum entropy does not account explicitly for the distance between the nuclei, which contrasts to the total energy calculation where the energy minimum depends decisively on that distance. The numerically exact and the time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo calculations show close results.

authors.name: Ivan P. Christov

papers.title: Doubling Efficiency of Hamiltonian Simulation via Generalized Quantum Signal Processing
papers.summary: Quantum signal processing provides an optimal procedure for simulating Hamiltonian evolution on a quantum computer using calls to a block encoding of the Hamiltonian. In many situations it is possible to control between forward and reverse steps with almost identical cost to a simple controlled operation. We show that it is then possible to reduce the cost of Hamiltonian simulation by a factor of 2 using the recent results of generalised quantum signal processing.

authors.name: Dominic W. Berry, Danial Motlagh, Giacomo Pantaleoni, Nathan Wiebe

papers.title: Detailed assessment of calculating drag force with quantum computers: Explicit time-evolution precludes exponential advantage for nonlinear differential equations
papers.summary: This study examines the potential for fault-tolerant quantum computers to provide utility in fluid dynamics simulations, with a focus on drag force calculations for ship hull design. We assess whether quantum algorithms can surpass classical computational limits by generating detailed quantum resource estimates (QREs) in terms of logical qubits and $T$-gate counts. Our analysis is based on a quantum algorithm leveraging Carleman linearization of the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), which has been suggested to offer exponential speedup. We develop efficient block encodings for LBM matrices and a method for amplitude-encoding drag force. We apply the method to the simple case of fluid flow past a sphere across a range of Reynolds numbers ($\mathrm{Re}$). We estimate the required (logical qubits)$\times$($T$-gates), finding them to be prohibitively large, ranging from $10^{21}$ to $10^{39}$. While classical simulations scale as $O(\mathrm{Re}^3)$, our QREs exhibit a modest polynomial scaling of $O(\mathrm{Re}^{2.69})$, indicating no exponential quantum advantage. We attribute this limitation to an intrinsic power-law relationship between spatial grid resolution and time-stepping requirements that is a fundamental characteristic of explicit methods for evolving nonlinear differential equations. Thus, quantum computers are unlikely to provide utility in applications that require time-evolving fluids and other systems of nonlinear differential equations.

authors.name: John Penuel, Amara Katabarwa, Peter D. Johnson, Parker Kuklinski, Benjamin Rempfer, Collin Farquhar, Yudong Cao, Michael C. Garrett

papers.title: Quantum Power Method and Numerical Integration Using Quantum Singular Value Transformation
papers.summary: Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) is a framework that has been shown to unify many primitives in quantum algorithms. In this work, we leverage the QSVT framework in two directions. We first revisit one recently introduced quantum power method within the QSVT framework and implement its matrix powers with block encodings, which makes the cost of this subroutine polylogarithmic in the inverse precision; the overall running time, however, remains exponential in the number of power iterations because of post-selection. Additionally, we incorporate several elementary numerical integration techniques, such as the rectangular method, Monte Carlo method, and quadrature method, into the QSVT framework, which results in polynomial speedup with respect to the size or the number of points of the grid for the rectangular and quadrature rules, compared with exact classical summation over the grid. Our results thus provide further examples to demonstrate the potential of the QSVT and how it may enhance quantum algorithmic tasks.

authors.name: Nhat A. Nghiem, Hiroki Sukeno, Shuyu Zhang, Tzu-Chieh Wei

papers.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Lindbladians for Quantum Stochastic Thermodynamics
papers.summary: We develop a thermodynamically consistent Lindblad approach for quantum stochastic thermodynamics, where each bath dissipator satisfies the local quantum detailed balance condition. We formulate the thermodynamic geometry to determine the optimal protocol in the slow-driving regime. Thermodynamic consistency leads to the joint fluctuation theorem for quantum work and heat, with the corresponding joint statistics obtained from a tilted master equation and generally described by a quasiprobability. We apply this framework to the quantum Brownian motion master equation, refining it to satisfy detailed balance, deriving optimal protocols at different temperatures and friction coefficients, and studying the work statistics. Our approach thus enables the study of nonequilibrium thermodynamics in open quantum systems.

authors.name: Jin-Fu Chen

papers.title: Quantum Metrology in Transmission Electron Microscopy
papers.summary: Quantum metrology experiments in atomic physics and quantum optics have demonstrated measurement accuracy beyond the shot-noise limit via multi-particle entanglement. At the same time, electron microscopy -- an essential tool for high-resolution imaging across many fields of science and technology from materials to life sciences -- is severely constrained in its signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by shot noise, due to the dose limit imposed by electron beam-induced damage. Here, we show theoretically that quantum metrology methods based on electron entanglement are a natural fit for improving the SNR in electron microscopy. We investigate the generation of the necessary entangled states through electron-electron Coulomb interactions and quantum non-demolition measurements. Our results connect the fields of quantum metrology and electron interferometry, paving the way toward electron microscopy with SNR beyond the shot-noise limit.

authors.name: Shiran Even-Haim, Ethan Nussinson, Roni Ben-Maimon, Alexey Gorlach, Ron Ruimy, Ephraim Shahmoon, Osip Schwartz, Ido Kaminer

papers.title: A shorter-width post-selected circuit for a truncated-Taylor Hamiltonian-evolution segment
papers.summary: We present an ancilla-efficient, post-selected circuit construction for a truncated-Taylor approximation to short-time Hamiltonian evolution. The construction combines a binary Taylor-order register with mid-circuit measurement, reset, and reuse of the Hamiltonian-index register. Conditioned on the prescribed all-zero outcomes, the circuit implements the truncated Taylor approximation while maintaining coherence among the Taylor-order branches while permitting early termination after a failed post-selection. For Taylor cutoff $K$, a Hamiltonian containing $L$ terms, and an $n$-qubit system, the circuit uses $\left\lceil\log {(K+1)}\right\rceil +\left\lceil\log L\right\rceil+n $ qubits, and executes $\mathcal{O}(K)$ controlled Hamiltonian blocks in a complete segment. We analyze its post-selection probability and expected per-segment cost, and implement and evaluate the construction in Guppy[1,2]. The present work focuses on the low-width implementation of individual short-time propagation segments; coherent composition into a deterministic long-time simulation requires an additional amplification or compression mechanism and is left for future work.

authors.name: Michelle Wynne Sze, David Zsolt Manrique, David Mu\~noz Ramo, Nathan Fitzpatrick

papers.title: Recursive Clifford noise reduction
papers.summary: Clifford noise reduction CliNR is a partial error correction scheme that reduces the logical error rate of Clifford circuits at the cost of a modest qubit and gate overhead. The CliNR implementation of an $n$-qubit Clifford circuit of size $s$ achieves a vanishing logical error rate if $snp^2\rightarrow 0$ where $p$ is the physical error rate. Here, we propose a recursive version of CliNR that can reduce errors on larger circuits with a relatively small gate overhead. When $np \rightarrow 0$, the logical error rate can be vanishingly small. When $sp >2$ this can be achieved with $\left(2\left\lceil \log(sp)\right\rceil+1\right)n+1$ qubits and at most $24 s \left\lceil(sp)^{3.6}\right\rceil $ gates. For $sp\le 2$ we recover the original CliNR. Using numerical simulations, we show that the recursive method can offer an advantage in a realistic near-term parameter regime. When circuit sizes are large enough, recursive CliNR can reach a lower logical error rate than the original CliNR with the same gate overhead. The results offer promise for reducing logical errors in large Clifford circuits with relatively small overheads.

authors.name: Aharon Brodutch, Gregory Baimetov, Edwin Tham, Nicolas Delfosse

papers.title: A slightly improved upper bound for quantum statistical zero-knowledge
papers.summary: The complexity class Quantum Statistical Zero-Knowledge ($\mathsf{QSZK}$), introduced by Watrous (FOCS 2002) and later refined in Watrous (SICOMP, 2009), has the best known upper bound $\mathsf{QIP(2)} \cap \text{co-}\mathsf{QIP(2)}$, which was simplified following the inclusion $\mathsf{QIP(2)} \subseteq \mathsf{PSPACE}$ established in Jain, Upadhyay, and Watrous (FOCS 2009). Here, $\mathsf{QIP(2)}$ denotes the class of promise problems that admit two-message quantum interactive proof systems in which the honest prover is typically computationally unbounded, and $\text{co-}\mathsf{QIP(2)}$ denotes the complement of $\mathsf{QIP(2)}$. We slightly improve this upper bound to $\mathsf{QIP(2)} \cap \text{co-}\mathsf{QIP(2)}$ with a quantum linear-space honest prover. Specifically, the honest prover uses space linear in the size of the transcript of the original $\mathsf{QSZK}$ proof system. A similar improvement also applies to the upper bound for the non-interactive variant $\mathsf{NIQSZK}$. Our main techniques are algorithmic versions of the Holevo-Helstrom measurement and the Uhlmann transform, both implementable in quantum linear space, implying polynomial-time complexity in the state dimension, using the recent space-efficient quantum singular value transformation of Le Gall, Liu, and Wang (CC, 2026). We also establish that our linear-space bounds for these two tasks are near-optimal under the counting version of the Satisfiability Hypothesis (#SH).

authors.name: Fran\c{c}ois Le Gall, Yupan Liu, Qisheng Wang

papers.title: Hybrid non-degenerate parametric amplifier for a microwave cavity mode and an NV ensemble
papers.summary: We introduce an implementation of a non-degenerate parametric amplifier in which the signal and idler modes, respectively, a microwave mode and an ensemble of spins (e.g., nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond), are operated in their linear regime. This paramp, which amplifies signals in both parts at room and cryogenic temperatures, can be used to generate both the two-mode and single-mode squeezing of either system. It requires merely modulating the frequency of the spin ensemble at the sum of the cavity and spin frequencies (providing the classical pump) with the two systems sufficiently detuned. This effect is remarkable given that modulating a spin ensemble by itself produces neither amplification nor squeezing, unlike modulating an oscillator, and that an off-resonant perturbative analysis would suggest that modulating the spin ensemble merely parametrically drives the cavity mode. With typical cavity parameters including a cavity quality factor~$Q=10^4$, and a 1 GHz modulation amplitude, the microwave signal can be amplified by approximately $18~\mbox{dB}$ in $1.7~\mbox{$\mu$s}$, with a resonant bandwidth of about $0.5~\mbox{MHz}$. At $10~\mbox{mK}$ with the same modulation amplitude and a cavity and spin $Q=5\times 10^4$ it generates approximately $5~\mbox{dB}$ of squeezing. We also examine the experimental requirements for implementation.

authors.name: Roman Ovsiannikov, Kurt Jacobs, Andrii G. Sotnikov, Matthew E. Trusheim, Denys I. Bondar

papers.title: Loss-insensitive reduction of amplified quantum noise in a Raman amplifier with coherent feedback
papers.summary: A quantum amplifier usually adds extra noise inevitably through coupling to internal degrees of freedom while amplifying the signal. The introduction of quantum correlations can effectively suppress this extra noise. In this work, we utilize the established quantum correlation between the Stokes field and atomic spin waves in the Raman amplification process to feed back a portion of the Stokes field into the amplifier. This leads to a reduction in amplified quantum noise that is independent of the feedback loss at high gain. A maximum of 6 dB noise reduction is observed. The single-path feedback amplifier is found to be sensitive to the feedback phase due to quantum interference, and we experimentally demonstrate an improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio of $4.4\pm 0.7$dB for a phase signal encoded in the feedback loop compared to the case without feedback. This general concept can be extended to integrated optics and fiber-optic systems with potential applications in quantum precision measurement.

authors.name: Jianmin Wang, Rong Zhu, Z. Y. Ou

papers.title: Time-dependent adiabatic elimination in matter-wave optics
papers.summary: We show how the dynamics of a specific subset of states can be separated from the dynamic of the total quantum state via a time-dependent projector-based formalism of adiabatic elimination. Within our formalism, we assume explicit time dependency in the coupling between both subsystems. Additionally, we do not assume that the elements of the Hamiltonian commute, as in matter-wave optics this not given in general. Here the center-of-mass degrees of freedom frequently need to be taken into account. Our formalism allows to perform the adiabatic elimination in such a setting.

authors.name: Samuel B\"ohringer, Alexander Bott, Eric P. Glasbrenner

papers.title: Universal Hamiltonian control in a planar trimon circuit
papers.summary: Multimode circuits provide an avenue for flexible control of single and multi-qubit gates. In this work we implement a multimode circuit known as a trimon integrated in a planar geometry. The trimon features three transmon-like modes with strong all-to-all $ZZ$ coupling. We demonstrate high fidelity operations on the trimon, achieving flexible control of its rich state space. This includes qubit rotations conditioned on one or both other qubits, unconditional single-qubit rotations, and both excitation-conserving and double-excitation two-qubit entangling gates. Through multi-tone driving we are able to implement all 16 two-qubit Pauli operators in the two-qubit space. We further demonstrate using the trimon as a qudit with up to 8 states and higher coherence than typical transmon-based implementations. Our results show a compact, highly controllable device that can potentially replace transmons in standard superconducting processor architectures.

authors.name: Vivek Maurya, Daria Kowsari, Kumar Saurav, S. A. Shanto, R. Vijay, Daniel A. Lidar, Eli M. Levenson-Falk

papers.title: Analog entanglement distillation through Hamiltonian scrambling
papers.summary: Efficient entanglement distillation is a central primitive for quantum information processing and future quantum networks. Conventional protocols rely on digital quantum circuits, requiring compiled multi-qubit gate sequences and fine-grained control that place heavy demands on near-term hardware. Crucially, leading network platforms, such as trapped ions and neutral atoms, naturally support coherent many-body interactions suited for continuous-time analog evolution. Motivated by this, we introduce the Hamiltonian entanglement distillation protocol, which uses information scrambling under native dynamics for analog quantum error detection. We establish a quantitative link between out-of-time-order correlators and distillation performance, showing that efficient scrambling directly yields high output fidelity. This capability is generic across interacting many-body Hamiltonians, with typical random Hamiltonians achieving near-optimal error detection in a constant evolution time independent of system size. Extending this framework to entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD), we show that analog error detection combined with classical post-processing saturates the fundamental 33.3% depolarizing noise-tolerance bound. Numerical simulations of device-native Rydberg-atom and trapped-ion Hamiltonians confirm that high-fidelity distillation is achievable within current experimental coherence times. Together, these results establish native analog dynamics as a practical, low-overhead route to entanglement distillation on near-term quantum platforms.

authors.name: Zitai Xu, Guoding Liu, Xingjian Zhang

papers.title: Climbing the Clifford Hierarchy
papers.summary: The Clifford Hierarchy has been a central topic in quantum computation due to its strong connections with fault-tolerant quantum computation, magic state distillation, and more. Nevertheless, only sections of the hierarchy are fully understood, such as diagonal gates and third level gates. The diagonal part of the hierarchy can be climbed by taking square roots and adding controls. Similarly, square roots of Pauli gates (first level) are Clifford gates (climb to the second level). Based on this theme, we study gates whose square roots climb to the next level. In this paper, we primarily focus on Hermitian gates, and in particular, we fully characterize Hermitian Clifford gates whose square roots climb to the third level.

authors.name: Luca Bastioni, Akash Bhople, Samuel Glandon, Tefjol Pllaha, Madison Stewart, Phillip Waitkevich

papers.title: Sharp Entropy Cost of Coherent Leakage Across a Block Decomposition
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal{H}=P\mathcal{H}\oplus Q\mathcal{H}$ and let $\Pi\rho=P\rho P\oplus Q\rho Q$ be the two-block pinching of a density matrix. We study the block-coherence entropy $D(\rho\|\Pi\rho)$, the relative-entropy cost of removing cross-block coherence. First, we prove a midpoint Bogoliubov--Kubo--Mori (BKM) coercivity estimate, giving the operator-kernel lower bound $D(\rho\|\Pi\rho)\ge \operatorname{Tr}[B^*\Omega_{A,C}^{-1}(B)]$ for strictly positive diagonal blocks. The proof uses the block-sign involution $U=P-Q$ to obtain a sign-symmetric midpoint lower bound for the BKM Hessian. Second, we solve the associated constrained entropy-minimization problem: at fixed protected-sector floor, leakage mass, and quadratic coherence, the minimum can be achieved by a single active two-level block, independently of the ambient dimension. Third, under a uniform floor $A\ge a_0P$ and $0<\varepsilon_Q\le a_0/2$, we recover the logarithmic boundary law $D(\rho\|\Pi\rho)\ge\|B\|_F^2\log(a_0/\varepsilon_Q)$, showing a divergent entropy cost per unit quadratic coherence as leakage mass tends to zero. As a finite-dimensional application, the estimates give an entropy certificate for coherent leakage from a protected subspace: $P\rho Q$ measures protected--leakage coherence, and the constrained entropy minimum is attained by a state supported on a single effective two-level transition. The BKM estimate also yields a dissipation lower bound along an idealized uniform block-dephasing orbit. Finally, the midpoint mechanism extends to finite-dimensional trace-preserving $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded automorphisms and finite von Neumann algebras under bounded uniform positivity assumptions.

authors.name: Hassan Nasreddine

papers.title: Perturbative results of fractional quantum mechanics for two particular systems
papers.summary: The fractional Schr\"odinger equation is studied with a kinetic energy that slightly deviates from the usual nonrelativistic form. The harmonic oscillator and the Kepler problem are both treated in the context of small perturbations. The usual perturbation theory is used and compared with the envelope theory. The corrections to the unperturbed Hamiltonians are analytical. The bounds computed with the envelope theory are good for the harmonic oscillator but not quite as good for the Kepler problem.

authors.name: Claude Semay, Clara Tourbez, Lo\"ic Keszeli

papers.title: Microscopic exceptional points in the post-selected open Jaynes--Cummings model
papers.summary: Phenomenological non-Hermitian Hamiltonians track selected signatures of complex reservoir dynamics, while post-selected no-jump effective Hamiltonians derived from microscopic open-system theory reveal the underlying system--reservoir physics. We derive the conditioned Jaynes--Cummings spectrum and propagator at finite temperature using Moore--Penrose normalized generators on the full Hilbert space. Within the Born--Markov approximation, full Bohr-frequency resolution excludes exceptional points; partial resolution permits coalescence when transition splittings compete with relaxation and the reservoir responses vary negligibly over the coupled transitions. For zero-temperature examples on shifted resonance, where the bare detuning compensates the reservoir-induced differential Lamb shift, unequal independent losses produce an excitation-dependent threshold, while equal shared losses with vanishing cross Lamb shifts and an orthogonal coupling phase produce a threshold independent of excitation number within the partial-resolution regime. Our shared-loss examples show oscillatory conditional transfer below the common threshold, monotonic transfer toward unit population at it, and a lower asymptotic population above it.

authors.name: B. M. Rodr\'iguez-lara

papers.title: Liouvillian Geometry of Multidimensional Spectra: Pathway Transport and Local Response Deformation
papers.summary: Liouville pathways provide the conceptual foundation for interpreting multidimensional spectroscopies but, in open quantum systems, need not remain independent under the reduced dynamics. Environmental interactions can transport amplitude between pathway sectors during free evolution, producing measurable changes in the nonlinear response. We develop a differential framework for describing this transport under parametric deformation of the open-system dynamics. When the environment selects a pointer basis distinct from the observational basis, the resulting basis incompatibility mixes Liouville pathways and produces characteristic spectral distortions. Using a Duhamel expansion of the Liouvillian propagator, we derive local response derivatives that reconstruct this pathway redistribution. For a two-level model with a rotated dephasing basis, a second-order expansion about a single reference point retains the dominant spectral structure over a broad range of basis \Rconcept{misalignment, while the global error grows to approximately $37\%$ at maximal misalignment. These results show how local response information captures the spectroscopic consequences of Liouvillian deformation and establish pathway transport as a complementary organizing principle for multidimensional spectroscopy.

authors.name: Eric R. Bittner, Carlos Silva-Acu\~na, Hao Li

papers.title: How additional labels affect multiparticle indistinguishability of identical particles
papers.summary: For two identical particles, adding labels reduces the total overlap of their label states and decreases their exchange indistinguishability as measured by Hong--Ou--Mandel interference. For more than two particles, the opposite effect can occur: introducing additional labels can boost multiparticle indistinguishability. We present an explicit seven-particle example in which additional labels increase multiparticle indistinguishability by $7.38\%$, as quantified by the symmetric projection weight of the seven-particle label state, while decreasing the mean squared pairwise overlap by nearly half. We trace this effect to the cancellation of collective multiparticle phases. Phases associated with one set of label states cancel those associated with the other, thereby turning destructive contributions to the symmetric weight into constructive ones. We also give sufficient conditions that rule out this effect. For any number of identical particles, additional label states independent of the original label states cannot increase indistinguishability when the original symmetric weight is at least $1/2$. Independent additional label states also cannot increase the symmetric weight of any number of identical particles prepared independently in the same mixed label state.

authors.name: Valery Shchesnovich

papers.title: Insecurity of Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution
papers.summary: The security of practical quantum key distribution (QKD) systems is fundamentally constrained by vulnerabilities of single-photon detectors. Measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) was proposed to remove this limitation by allowing all measurements to be performed by a completely untrusted party, under the assumption that the measurement node can be treated as adversarial but does not compromise the security guarantees of the protocol. Here we show that this assumption is insufficient under realistic adversarial control of the measurement device. We present an attack in which an adversary exploits active control of the measurement node (Charlie) to obtain significant information about the secret key. The attack enables recovery of up to 70\% of the sifted key while introducing only 5.6\% quantum bit error rate. Unlike previously reported attacks targeting specific implementations of MDI-QKD, our results demonstrate a limitation of the standard security model underlying the protocol. These findings indicate that additional constraints on the measurement-device independence assumption, or refined security analyses incorporating stronger adversarial capabilities, are required to ensure the security of MDI-QKD in realistic scenarios.

authors.name: Konstantin Zaitsev, Polina Acheva

papers.title: Electrons Hopping across a Molecular Network: Spectra and Symmetries
papers.summary: We investigate interacting spinless electrons on finite molecular networks described by a tight-binding Hubbard Hamiltonian. The interplay between network geometry, Coulomb interactions and discrete symmetries is analysed for rings with $L=3,4,5,6$ nodes, filled with one, two or three electrons. Special attention is devoted to the role of the network symmetries in determining the structure of the many-body spectrum and the Mulliken classification of the eigenstates. Using group-theoretical methods, we examine the evolution of the spectra in the presence of an external magnetic flux. The Zeeman effect lifts degeneracies and results in combination with the Coulomb interaction to avoided crossings in symmetry sectors. We identify a qualitatively distinction between systems with an even and odd number of particles. At half-filling, particle-hole symmetry (duality) protects selected symmetry sectors against Zeeman splitting.

authors.name: Ludwig Schulz, Max Best, Carsten Henkel

papers.title: A Performance Model for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Workflows
papers.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical workflows are expected to underpin practical quantum computing, yet the community lacks a shared framework for reasoning about integration requirements. We introduce a runtime model that decomposes workflow execution into quantum compute, classical compute, and communication costs at two levels of analysis. At the application level, where communication overhead only affects performance, we use a communication-to-computation ratio to quantify its impact on runtime. At the real-time level, when communication overhead determines feasibility, we examine how decoding and feedback latency affect logical operation times and resource requirements. The model evaluates execution with allocated resources, excluding scheduling and resource management. Applied to representative workflows, it shows that the compute-intensive applications, including those requiring HPC resources, are largely insensitive to communication overhead. However, the model identifies when hardware evolution, such as faster quantum processing and greater parallelism, can shift this balance toward communication bottlenecks.
