Notably, the WF combined with joint shaping achieves the best ISAC trade-off. Low-complexity PAS variants closely approach this performance, offering a flexible trade-off and outperforming legacy modulation formats.

authors.name: Benedikt Geiger, Daniel Gil Gaviria, Christian Karle, Delcho Donev, Charlotte Muth, Thomas Zwick, J\"urgen Becker, Benjamin Nuss, Laurent Schmalen

papers.title: N-1 Security constrained Hosting Capacity Assessment for Ultra Large-scale Data Center with Workload Flexibility
papers.summary: Transmission network security can substantially alter where large-scale data centers can connect and how much workload flexibility can unlock. This paper develops a hosting-capacity framework that couples computing demand, batch workload scheduling, and N-1 security constraints. A modified IEEE 118-bus case study reveals that two data center sites with identical hosting capacities under normal operation differ by 874.5 MW under the contingencies operation when workload flexibility is enabled. Six-hour batch deferral increases N-1 hosting capacity by up to 24.5\% relative to immediate execution. These gains arise from reducing demand at critical hours while accommodating deferred tasks within subsequent transmission limits and deadlines. At bus 92, a four-hour window captures 90.9\% of the six-hour capacity gain. The findings establish workload flexibility as a location-dependent connection resource whose capacity value requires joint assessment of contingency exposure and deadline constrainted workload recovery, beyond the power reduction available at a single critical hour.

authors.name: Jiakai Wu, Pengyu Ren, Yifan Wang, Wei Sun

papers.title: Risk-Aware Safe Hierarchical Learning for Robust eMBB-URLLC Resource Allocation in O-RAN
papers.summary: Joint resource allocation for enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB) and ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) must satisfy stringent URLLC latency and reliability requirements while maintaining eMBB throughput under uncertain traffic and channel conditions. Existing learning-based allocators often optimize average aggregate performance without explicitly accounting for prediction errors, potentially resulting in severe service degradation for individual users. We propose a risk-aware safe hierarchical learning framework for Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) that learns resource-feasible allocations using service-cost penalties and a per-user URLLC service test. A non-real-time policy determines slice-level resource-block and power budgets, near-real-time policies allocate resource blocks and transmit power among users, and an execution-time safety layer checks per-user URLLC service and corrects allocations through bounded resource transfers when feasible. A deterministic per-user service test, derived using protected rates accounting for channel state information prediction errors and conformal upper bounds on traffic demand, ensures satisfaction of the probabilistic URLLC requirement. Service-specific conditional value-at-risk objectives prioritize users with the highest URLLC deadline-miss ratios and lowest eMBB rates. Experimental results show that, under nominal load, the proposed framework is the only evaluated method that satisfies both the URLLC deadline-miss target and worst-user eMBB rate criterion on average. It reduces the mean miss ratio by 64% relative to the best baseline in this metric and achieves the highest worst-user eMBB rate.

authors.name: Mohammad Hussain, Dilara Gurer, Gokhan Kalem, Sinem Coleri

papers.title: Quantifying the hosting capacity value of workload flexibility for AI data centers: A two-stage electricity-computation co-optimization framework
papers.summary: Grid connection constraints increasingly limit the expansion of AI data centers, yet the additional hosting capacity enabled by computational workload flexibility remains insufficiently quantified. This paper develops a two-stage electricity--computation co-optimization framework to quantify the individual and coordinated hosting capacity values of spatial and temporal workload flexibility. Data center capacities are determined endogenously, with computational task arrivals scaling with admitted capacity. Spatial routing of eligible interactive requests and temporal deferral of batch workloads are linked to server operation and facility power demand, subject to workload completion requirements and transmission constraints. The first stage maximizes aggregate hosting capacity; the second fixes the resulting site capacities and optimizes annual workload scheduling and generation dispatch to minimize generation and carbon costs. An 8760-hour case study with three data centers on a modified IEEE 118-bus system shows that temporal and spatial flexibility individually increase hosting capacity by 21.26\% and 5.37\%, respectively. Their coordinated use raises hosting capacity from 4635.1~MW to 6231.5~MW, a 34.44\% increase without network reinforcement. The coordinated gain exceeds the sum of the individual gains by 361.9~MW, demonstrating complementarity between spatial migration and temporal deferral. By redistributing computational demand across locations and operating hours, these mechanisms enable fuller utilization of existing transmission capacity. The findings establish workload flexibility as a quantifiable planning resource for accommodating additional data center capacity within existing transmission networks.

authors.name: Jiakai Wu, Wei Sun, Pengyu Ren, Yifan Wang

papers.title: Slim-Mamba: An Efficient and Reconfigurable Mamba-Based Accelerator for Massive MIMO Indoor Localization
papers.summary: Using real-world massive MIMO measurements from the LuViRA dataset, we present a system-level solution combining Mamba-based model development and hardware acceleration for indoor localization. Three Mamba-based models are explored: the original Mamba architecture, CMamba, a channel-correlation-enhanced state-space model designed to exploit correlations across input channels, and our proposed Slim-Mamba. Hardware implementation and bottleneck analysis are then used to guide further model simplification and optimization. The resulting Slim-Mamba simplifies the original Mamba selective state-space block into a lightweight gated recurrent update, preserving temporal state modelling and output gating while reducing the complexity of the selective-scan computation. The deployed model contains 816k trainable parameters and has a model size of 3.40MB under FP32 precision while maintaining high localization accuracy. The corresponding accelerator provides a reconfigurable architecture with a highly parallel MAC array optimized for matrix-vector operations and fine-grained pipelining, improving resource utilization and reducing inference latency. The hardware-aware fixed-point model achieves a mean localization error of 0.14m, closely matching the floating-point baseline. Implemented on a Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU102 FPGA, the four-block backbone has an estimated serial latency of 212.04us per token at 100MHz.

authors.name: Shengjie Chen, Chenxi Zhang, Sijia Cheng, Ove Edfors, Liang Liu, Ilayda Yaman

papers.title: Data-driven control of polynomial systems using implicit methods
papers.summary: While conventional behavioral data-driven control represents linear time-invariant (LTI) systems directly from data, extending these data representations to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. We address this gap for general polynomial systems, characterizing their finite-length trajectories as a real algebraic variety defined by implicit polynomial relations rather than explicit equations. First, we provide conditions on measured data under which these data can be used to represent the system. Building on this representation, we formulate data-driven simulation and predictive control problems that are equivalent to their model-based counterparts, and solve the resulting polynomial systems globally using homotopy continuation. Numerical case studies confirm the effectiveness of this approach by successfully simulating a stiff Van der Pol oscillator in situations where explicit models fail. Furthermore, these data-driven simulation and control methods are illustrated on a Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that our method outperforms Koopman-based approaches in predicting long trajectories.

authors.name: Andr\'as Sasfi, Florian D\"orfler, Ivan Markovsky, Jaap Eising

papers.title: Data-Driven Factored Abstractions of Stochastic Systems
papers.summary: Formal verification and correct-by-design policy synthesis for stochastic dynamical systems face significant scalability challenges due to the curse of dimensionality. These challenges are exacerbated when the system dynamics are unknown and abstractions must be constructed from data. This paper introduces a data-driven framework for constructing factored interval Markov decision process (fIMDP) abstractions from noisy transition observations. Assuming conditional independence of successor coordinates and known coordinate-wise Lipschitz bounds on the dynamics, the framework estimates marginal transition probabilities rather than joint probabilities, resulting in an exponential reduction in the number of probability entries to be estimated and stored. We establish finite-sample confidence guarantees that the abstraction captures the concrete transition probabilities uniformly over each abstract region, enabling certified lower bounds on satisfaction probabilities for $\omega$-regular specifications. Experiments on benchmark systems, including pendulum swing-up, unicycle control, and a four-dimensional planar robot model, demonstrate improvements in certified satisfaction probability lower bounds of up to 25 percentage points compared with a state-of-the-art flat IMDP abstraction method. Our framework required up to 23x less memory and was consistently faster in constructing the abstraction.

authors.name: Mahdi Nazeri, Frederik Baymler Mathiesen, Sadegh Soudjani, Alessandro Abate

papers.title: Spectrally Correlated Frequency Spreading Codes for FRESH Filtering-based Interference Cancellation
papers.summary: Frequency shift (FRESH) filters can achieve co-channel interference cancellation by exploiting spectral correlation statistics of both the desired and interfering signals. In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, spectral correlation can be introduced in a structured way by symbol repetition across subcarriers. While this repetition generally requires duplicating symbols by an integer multiple of 2+ times (significantly impacting spectral efficiency), in this work it is shown that applying an incomplete spreading code, that trades spectral efficiency, to the desired signal can control its spectral correlation properties at redundancy factors less than 2. The distribution of the spectral correlation across frequencies determines the level of protection against interference at a given frequency. We introduce the design of frequency spreading codes that provide uniform spectral correlation distribution across frequencies, which provides equal interference cancellation capability independent of the center frequency of the interfering signal. The introduced spreading code can achieve arbitrary code rates while possessing two important properties: 1) semi-orthogonality and 2) spectral correlation uniformity. We evaluate the BER performance at very low signal-to-interference levels SIR$=0, 5 $ dB comparing spreading, LDPC, and LDPC+spreading at equal code rates.

authors.name: Karim Said, Xinrui Li, Daniel J. Jakubisin, Jeffrey H. Reed

papers.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
papers.summary: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. First, we establish the S-SM-NR framework by formulating the joint design of the task graph and the transmit-listen schedule. Then, we analyze the minimum round count required by S-SM-NR and establish a connectivity condition for network localization. Subsequently, we develop a closed-form joint design that constructs the sparse task graph and the balanced transmit-listen schedule. In particular, the joint design can achieve the minimum round count under the complete physical connectivity. Finally, simulations show that the proposed S-SM-NR scheme reduces the occupied-round count and improves the localization accuracy by shortening the ranging cycle.

authors.name: Zijian Zhang, Yuan Shen

papers.title: Hierarchical Traffic Engineering for Scalable Software-Defined Satellite Networks
papers.summary: Future satellite systems are shifting toward regenerative payloads that interconnect many modem banks into a reconfigurable on-board network. However, conventional constellation-level routing overlooks intra-payload congestion and load imbalance, which can limit the traffic each satellite can accommodate. This paper proposes a hierarchical software-defined networking (SDN)framework for traffic engineering (TE) across both the constellation and payload levels. The system is represented by a two-level graph, where each satellite node in the constellation graph is expanded into an internal network of interconnected modem banks. The proposed hierarchical payload-aware allocation (HPAA) algorithm coordinates the two levels through the exchange of assigned traffic demand and advertised capacity budgets. Simulation results show that, under heavy load, HPAA delivers about 9 times the throughput of shortest-path routing, with 17% lower end-to-end delay and no packet loss. These findings highlight that hierarchical control accounting for the on-board network constraints of regenerative payloads is a key lever to improve the performance of satellite constellations.

authors.name: Mohamed Khiari, Wiem Abderrahim, Olfa Ben Yahia, Fatma Abdelkefi, Wessam Ajib, Gunes Karabulut Kurt

papers.title: Greedy Vector Approximation Based on Rotation for Multiplierless Complex Products
papers.summary: This paper proposes a greedy approximation algorithm for performing complex-valued inner products in multiplierless hardware. The matching pursuits for accurate rotation approximation (MPARA) algorithm approximates the tangent of the phase of complex elements as a sum of signed powers of two (SOPOT) representation, enabling multiplierless hardware for complex-valued multiplication. The proposed algorithm outperforms other state-of-the-art approximation methods for approximating the twiddle factors of a fast Fourier transform (FFT).

authors.name: Luiz F. da S. Coelho, Paulo S. R. Diniz, Didier Le Ruyet

papers.title: AMISS: An Integrity Framework for Magnetic Navigation
papers.summary: Magnetic Navigation (MagNav) is a promising alternative to traditional systems like Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), offering resistance to jamming or spoofing attacks to which the latter are vulnerable. MagNav matches scalar magnetic measurements over time against a known map of Earth's magnetic anomaly in order to position a vehicle. MagNav is therefore sensitive to the quality of these maps, especially to errors in the survey data that the maps are derived from. In order to be a reliable and mature navigation technology, MagNav must satisfy integrity requirements for mitigation of such faults. To this end, a solution-separation monitoring algorithm is developed that performs a role equivalent to Advanced Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (ARAIM) in GNSS, which detects faults as well as generates worst-case bounds (protection levels) on estimation error for faults too small to be detected. It is shown how these integrity methods can be developed in a \emph{windowed-in-time} sense, where subsets of measurements over a time window are compared with each other in order to detect outliers that can potentially result from errors in the map. The applicability of the approach is demonstrated using results obtained using synthetic aircraft data with injected faults.

authors.name: Sharad C. Shankar, Prasenjit Sengupta, J. Scott Clawson, Sam Pullen

papers.title: Structure-Behavior Coalescence: A Definition of Systems
papers.summary: For more than seventy years, systems engineering has developed extensive models and frameworks, yet the fundamental question of what constitutes a system remains insufficiently formalized. Existing approaches often treat structure and behavior as separate aspects, leaving their unity, system identity, and consistency conditions insufficiently defined. This paper introduces Structure-Behavior Coalescence (SBC) as a formal framework that defines a system as an integrated entity in which structure and behavior are coalesced through interaction. SBC provides a formal modeling approach with well-formedness constraints for maintaining structural-behavioral coherence, including representations for terminal, paused, and intermediate states and rules for sequential, parallel, and alternative behaviors. The framework provides a formal perspective on the question, "What is a system?", and establishes a foundation for consistent system modeling, verification, and analysis.

authors.name: William S. Chao

papers.title: Structure-Behavior Coalescence for Model-Based Systems Engineering
papers.summary: Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) has advanced system design and analysis for decades, yet traditional approaches often treat structure and behavior separately, resulting in inconsistencies, incomplete models, and ambiguity. This paper introduces Structure-Behavior Coalescence (SBC) as a formal and unified definition of systems for MBSE. SBC defines a system as a single integrated entity in which structure and behavior are coalesced through interaction, providing both a conceptual foundation and a formal process-algebra framework. Well-formedness constraints ensure that interactions are structurally grounded and compositions are valid, enabling consistency by construction. Boundary processes, including 0 for terminal states and a checkpoint construct for paused or suspended states, allow inactive and intermediate states to be represented while preserving system unity. Illustrative examples and a Smart Healthcare IoT case study demonstrate how SBC supports sequential, parallel, and alternative behaviors while maintaining structural-behavioral coherence. SBC provides a foundation for formal verification, compositional modeling, and systematic inconsistency detection, connecting a rigorous definition of systems with practical MBSE applications.

authors.name: William S. Chao

papers.title: Plug-and-Play Sensor Evolution in Software-Defined Vehicles through Asset Administration Shells
papers.summary: Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) promise continuous software evolution, but sensor integration in deployed vehicles still depends on manual configuration, hardware-specific drivers, and repeated application-side adaptation. Existing standards address only parts of this problem. AUTOSAR standardizes selected sensor interfaces, the Vehicle Signal Specification (VSS) standardizes signal semantics, and Asset Administration Shells (AAS) standardize digital asset descriptions. However, these building blocks are rarely combined into an end-to-end onboarding path for sensors attached after vehicle deployment. This paper presents an AAS-driven plug-and-play sensor integration framework for safety-supervised sensors. Each sensor is represented by an AAS that combines hardware identification, interface metadata, VSS mappings, and references to containerized driver and optional application software. After physical connection, an edge gateway identifies the device, retrieves the matching AAS, deploys the referenced software, and publishes the resulting data under stable vehicle signal paths. A prototype on a resource-constrained edge gateway connected to an RR100 UGV demonstrates automated integration of a USB camera and an ultrasonic sensor. Across repeated integration cycles, the prototype reaches operational state in about 2s, shows no failed events, and keeps applications independent of hardware-specific interfaces. The results indicate that the introduction of AAS as an executable onboarding contract enables automated runtime deployment of sensor drivers in SDV environments.

authors.name: Akshay Narla, Nasser Jazdi, Michael Weyrich

papers.title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: We introduce TAG (Testbed for Autonomous Games), a compact, low-cost robotic platform for studying learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG combines an actively tilted and steered ball-in-maze board with a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum. The pendulum's reaction torque and vibration disturb the board and marble, while the board's tilt, driven by the maze-solving policy, simultaneously disturbs the pendulum's balance. The main challenge in learning control policies for each subsystem is accounting for the impact of one subsystem's dynamics on the other's learning process. To address this challenge, we present complementary reinforcement learning paradigms, leveraging model-based and model-free approaches to learn the control policies for the maze and pendulum, respectively. Our key finding is that introducing the pendulum causes an immediate, sharp drop in the maze policy's success rate, but the policy adapts online and recovers to its pre-coupling performance within a small number of learning episodes. Experimental results show that both policies, trained independently, successfully control the maze board and the pendulum despite their physical coupling.

authors.name: Bao Trung Truong, Dat Thanh Nguyen, Thinh T. Doan

papers.title: SPICE: Stochastic Policy for Interaction in Cluttered Environments
papers.summary: Agricultural tasks such as harvesting and pruning require robots to reach through dense foliage, where contact is often unavoidable and vision is obstructed. Intermittent contact creates an imbalance between free-space and contact-rich observations, complicating the learning of contact-responsive behaviours. We present SPICE, a tactileconditioned diffusion policy for reaching targets in dense plant canopies using tactile sensing as the sole environmental feedback. SPICE exhibits three behaviours: moving through compliant foliage, manoeuvring around partially obstructing stems, and manipulating branches that block the target path. To the best of our knowledge, SPICE is the first tactile-conditioned diffusion policy for target reaching through physically cluttered plant canopies. Across over 180 real-robot trials, SPICE was evaluated against tactile-conditioned, image-conditioned, and reactive-control baselines. Spatial tactile information and explicit contact conditioning proved important, with SPICE achieving 95% branch-manoeuvring success versus 45% for the strongest tactile baseline. SPICE also achieved branch manipulation beyond the reactive controller and remained effective under visual occlusion, where the image-conditioned DP failed. Zero-shot transfer across 40 trials on unseen tomato and lime plants achieved 87.5% success rate. These results demonstrate the potential of tactile-conditioned generative policies for interaction in visually occluded plant environments.

authors.name: Nidhi Parayil, Benjamin Greenland, Thierry Peynot, Chris Lehnert

papers.title: Recoverability, Not Invariance: Certified Safety for Robots at the Limits of Performance
papers.summary: Safety certification in robotics typically rests on forward invariance of the deployed controller, a property that demands high-fidelity models at the edge of the operating envelope, exactly where models are least reliable and robots perform best. As a result, many of the behaviors we most want robots to run, from learned policies to aggressive maneuvers at the limits of traction, cannot be certified at all. We introduce recoverability, a contraction-theoretic safety concept that resolves this tension by certifying a robot's ability to reengage a trusted recovery mode rather than the invariance of a deployed behavior. We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. To decide when to switch, we derive the contraction insertion gradient, the first-order effect of a recovery insertion on the certificate, and embed it in a switching-time program in which feasibility alone guarantees safety and optimality only shapes performance. To supply the certificates, we develop sequential convex synthesis that monotonically grows the certified tube toward the exact viability kernel. We validate our approach in simulated quadrotor flight through uncertain obstacles, where it outperforms invariance-based safety filters, and in hardware deployments aboard a full-scale IndyNXT autonomous racecar, where it repeatedly recovers the car from an aggressive raceline at the limits of handling in the rain. Recoverability provides a certified exit strategy, extending formal safety guarantees to aggressive, learned, and experimental behaviors without requiring their invariance.

authors.name: Thomas A. Berrueta, Joshua D. Ibrahim, Gilchrist X. Johnson, John Lathrop, Soon-Jo Chung

papers.title: Averting `Gravity': Launch Control and the Limits of Collision Avoidance in Low Earth Orbit Operations
papers.summary: As large constellations fill low Earth orbit, the risk of a runaway collision cascade has become a central concern of space operations. Debris population models treat collision avoidance as a fixed input, although the capacity to screen potential collisions and plan maneuvers degrades as debris accumulates. Using a stylized multi-layer queueing network model, we show that collision avoidance capabilities that saturate as the in-custody fragment count increases, can make the orbital shell bistable, with a low-debris and a high-debris equilibrium, and hysteretic. This has two major operational consequences. First, leaving the high-debris equilibrium requires a large cut in launch rates. Second, in the low-debris equilibrium, fragment counts respond with a delay as the launch rate rises past a tipping point. Removing bistability is desirable, and we show that fragment count-indexed admission control can achieve this. The least restrictive such policy lengthens the lag, whereas an exponential tilt of this policy makes the fragment count track its equilibrium with a bounded lag. Furthermore, admitting more launches can reduce the rate of completed missions, and under a unimodality condition a threshold rule on the debris fragment count maximizes this rate at equilibrium.

authors.name: Aditya S. Gopalan, Harsha Honnappa

papers.title: Radar-Native Control Barrier Functions: Doppler Range Rate as a Measured Barrier Derivative
papers.summary: Safe control around dynamic obstacles requires information about both distance and relative motion. Range-based filters commonly reconstruct the required range rate from successive range measurements or from obstacle-state estimators, which can introduce estimator delay or sensitivity to range noise when obstacle motion changes. A frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar measures radial relative velocity directly through Doppler. We use this measurement as the derivative of an ego-centered range control barrier function (CBF) and obtain a closed-form filter on the robot's forward velocity. A measurement margin constructed from sensor error bounds accounts for errors in range, Doppler, ego velocity, and bearing. In 508 paired encounters within the platform's retreat capability, direct Doppler produces two buffer incursions, compared with 15 for a constant-acceleration and 25 for a constant-velocity Kalman filter. On a Unitree Go1, the controller stops at $0.777 \pm 0.015$ m against the predicted $0.758$ m and reacts to a farther approaching object while a nearer static return remains. The guarantee covers the longitudinal range channel under bounded measurement errors and continuously available detections. Direct Doppler removes the need to reconstruct range rate in the safety loop, reducing the delay between a change in obstacle motion and its effect on the safety command.

authors.name: Johannes Mootz, Hesam Mojtahedi, Reza Akhavian

papers.title: The Geometry of Mode Sampling in Reconfigurable MIMO Channel Extrapolation
papers.summary: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays acquire channels by distributing radiation modes across their antenna elements. Equal mode counts fix the observation budget while leaving a spatial sampling choice that directly affects reconstruction of unmeasured channels. We establish how this assignment enters the inverse problem through the receive aperture and the coupling between propagation paths. For an isolated path with calibrated positive real responses, the power-weighted variance of antenna positions completely characterizes the assignment dependence of the profiled angle information at fixed mode counts. We then construct layouts with identical weighted apertures and different path correlations, exposing a limitation of aperture-based design in multipath propagation. A paired simulation study evaluates balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling using a common estimator with per-detection joint angle refinement. Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are entirely unobserved, with improvements across nearly all tested scenes at high signal-to-noise ratio. When every mode is sampled, the mean benefit is more sensitive to rare large errors. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the spatial distribution of mode measurements to both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.

authors.name: Shaoyang Sun, Chongwen Huang

papers.title: Estimation-Aware Reachability
papers.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability computes the states from which a system can be kept safe under worst-case disturbances, but it assumes the state is known exactly, whereas real robots act on noisy estimates whose uncertainty evolves with their motion. We extend Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability to the robot's belief, estimate and uncertainty, treating unexpected measurements as a bounded adversary and enlarging the unsafe set by the current uncertainty, so that certified states are safe with a prescribed probability. The formulation is compatible with existing solvers. In simulation, the resulting safety filters nearly eliminate the collisions of certaintyequivalent HJ and are less conservative than equally safe uncertainty-padding baselines. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/HimanshuPaudel/Estimation-Aware-Reachability

authors.name: Himanshu Paudel, Javier Borquez

papers.title: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space
papers.summary: This paper introduces a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays. By integrating linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging, we recast classical methods - including Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC - into a single structure. We extend this framework to accommodate ESPRIT-type methods by treating the number of simultaneously predicted subarray channels as an additional dimension. Furthermore, we adapt this approach to non-Gaussian signals, establishing a parallel framework for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. As a practical application, we propose universal, J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that estimate spatial super- resolution spectra within a unified computational architecture. This architecture produces spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods and any intermediate variations.

authors.name: Sergey S. Kuzin

papers.title: CommDreamer: Radio-Geometric World Models for Mapless Cellular-Connected UAV Trajectory Planning
papers.summary: Reliable cellular connectivity and collision-free flight are essential for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations in low-altitude urban canyons, where dense 3D buildings obstruct flight clearance, shadow serving base stations, and create strong co-channel interference at street intersections. Existing planners either require prior 3D city meshes and channel knowledge maps unavailable onboard, or rely on model-free reinforcement learning with low sample efficiency and poor cross-city generalization. We propose CommDreamer, a mapless radio-geometric world model that fuses raw onboard 3D LiDAR scans, multicell cellular reports, and shift-invariant relative kinematics to jointly infer local obstacle clearance and directional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) dynamics. Using a categorical recurrent state-space model, CommDreamer compresses multimodal measurement histories into a coordinate-invariant latent belief, enabling the UAV to foresee deep shadow zones and train a lightweight online policy purely via multi-step latent imagination without prior maps or antenna patterns. Zero-shot evaluations across unseen urban morphologies in our open-source ray-tracing simulator, AeroCity-RT, show that CommDreamer converges within 150 episodes where model-free reinforcement learning fails to complete flights, achieving 100.0% mission success with zero collisions while lifting median route SINR to 8.02 dB and cutting effective SINR outage by over 50% relative to radio-blind world-model and reactive LiDAR baselines.

authors.name: Yuqi Ping, Tianhao Liang, Tingting Zhang

papers.title: Capacity-Aware Redistribution Control for Mitigation of Cascading Failures in Networks
papers.summary: This paper studies the control of irreversible cascading failures in networks with finite node capacities. Each node carries a nonnegative divisible quantity, referred to as load, and fails irreversibly when its load exceeds its capacity. The network dynamics are represented by topology-dependent row-stochastic matrices. When nodes fail, these matrices must be updated. However, directly deleting rows and columns corresponding to failed nodes can reduce the total load in the network. We therefore introduce a topology update that preserves unit row sums and quantifies any unserved load explicitly. We derive the resulting load-balance relation and a necessary and sufficient condition for lossless redistribution after simultaneous failures. Based on these results, we formulate a two-stage optimization problem: the first stage minimizes unserved load, and the second stage minimizes the highest capacity utilization among the surviving nodes. Simulations on grid and Barabasi-Albert networks show that, unlike the standard equal and residual-capacity redistribution approaches, the proposed method prevents secondary failures in all tested cases, with a tradeoff against served load on scale-free networks.

authors.name: Ujjwal Pratap, Christian A. Hans

papers.title: Gradient-Based Defensive Poisoning Against System Identification Attacks on Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.summary: AI-driven attacks learn the models of cyber-physical systems (CPS) by passively observing controller and plant signals, then use this knowledge to act covertly. Because covertness depends on the accuracy of the identified model, degrading that accuracy is a viable countermeasure. This work applies Adversarial Machine Learning as a defense, injecting small perturbations into the measurements the attacker observes to degrade an artificial neural network (ANN)-based system identification (SI) attack. The perturbations are derived from input gradients of several independently trained identification models, aggregated into a generalized perturbation, and confined to the transient regimes that carry most of the dynamic information. A sparsity parameter further restricts them to the most influential samples, with negligible cost in effectiveness. On a simulated DC motor networked control system, the proposed perturbations induce larger prediction errors than stochastic poisoning of equal root-mean-square magnitude, and the advantage widens as the magnitude grows. This limits the defense's operating range, which is intended for decoy environments such as CPS honeynets. Additional results indicate that the designed poisoning signals can also degrade N4SID-based system identification, providing evidence of their transferability beyond the ANN-based models originally targeted.

authors.name: Gon\c{c}alo Fernandes, Jos\'e Cec\'ilio, Victor Mattos, Daniel S. Menasch\'e, Amit Bhaya, Alan Oliveira de S\'a

papers.title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief
papers.summary: A team of skilled card players share no information amongst each other, and yet still are able to coordinate their play by watching the same players and reading the same tells. Autonomous systems have failed to exploit this logic, relying instead on explicit communication or complex state estimation schemes that can fail when it matters most. Without it, decentralized agents diverge in their world beliefs, and coordination collapses. Here we show that anchoring all agents to a single shared external actor, a common witness whose reactions encode team state, produces spontaneous, communication-free coordination. An allocentric belief network trained on witness behavior allows each agent to independently reconstruct full team state, keeping group beliefs consistent with no inter-agent exchange. Across five competitive environments allocentric belief alignment outperforms egocentric approaches in collective performance, and even scales to sixty-agent teams where standard methods fail. These results establish a new principle for collective intelligence: in the absence of communication, a shared gaze replaces a shared channel.

authors.name: Cameron Mehlman, Arjun Mulchandani, Hovik Grigoryan, Anurag Koyyada, Gregory Falco

papers.title: Chirp-Permuted AFDM: A Versatile and Multifunctional Waveform for 6G
papers.summary: We present a novel multicarrier waveform, termed chirp-permuted affine frequency division multiplexing (CP-AFDM), which introduces a unique chirp-permutation domain on top of the chirp subcarriers of the conventional AFDM. Rigorous analysis of the signal model and waveform properties demonstrates that the proposed CP-AFDM waveform preserves all core characteristics of affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) - including robustness to doubly-dispersive channels, peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC)-enabling full delay-Doppler representation - while introducing a new degree-of-freedom without any loss of these properties. Given this, by exploiting the vast chirp-permutation domain, two selected exemplary multifunctional applications are presented: an index modulation (IM) technique over the permutation domain which achieves significant spectral efficiency gains, and a physical-layer security scheme that ensures practically perfect security through permutation-based keying, without requiring additional transmit energy or signaling over-head. In all, these characteristics establish CP-AFDM as a highly attractive candidate for emerging sixth generation (6G) use cases demanding reliability, sensing-awareness, and multifunctionality.

authors.name: Hyeon Seok Rou, Hanvit Kim, Sunwoo Kim, Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu

papers.title: Audiobook-CC: Controllable Long-context Speech Generation for Multicast Audiobook
papers.summary: Existing text-to-speech systems predominantly focus on single-sentence synthesis and lack adequate contextual modeling as well as fine-grained performance control capabilities for generating coherent multicast audiobooks. To address these limitations, we propose a context-aware and emotion controllable speech synthesis framework specifically engineered for multicast audiobooks with three key innovations: a context mechanism for contextual consistency, a disentanglement paradigm to decouple style control from speech prompts for semantic consistency, and self-distillation to boost emotional expressiveness and instruction controllability. Experimental results show superior performance across the generation of narration, dialogue, and the whole chapter, significantly outperforming existing baselines. Ablation studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of our proposed methods. Demo samples can be found in https://semisemi-ux.github.io/

authors.name: Min Liu, JingJing Yin, Xiang Zhang, Jianhao Ye, Siyu Hao, Siwei Xia, Hongbin Zhou

papers.title: General formulation of an analytic, Lipschitz continuous control allocation for thrust-vectored controlled rigid bodies
papers.summary: This paper presents a general framework for solving the control allocation problem (CAP) in thrust-vector controlled rigid bodies with an arbitrary number of thrusters. Two novel solutions are proposed: a closed-form, Lipschitz continuous mapping that ensures smooth actuator orientation references, and a convex optimization formulation capable of handling practical actuator constraints such as thrust saturation and angular rate limits. Both methods leverage the nullspace structure of the allocation mapping to preserve control authority while generating sub-optimal yet practical solutions. The resulting approaches allow to arbitrary select a desired trade-off between Lipschitz continuity constants and energy efficiency loss. The effectiveness and generality of the proposed framework are demonstrated through numerical examples on a marine vessel and an aerial quadcopter.

authors.name: Frank Mukwege, Tam W. Nguyen, Emanuele Garone

papers.title: Affordable Data Collection System for UAVs Taxi Vibration Testing
papers.summary: Structural vibration testing plays a key role in aerospace engineering for evaluating dynamic behaviour, ensuring reliability and verifying structural integrity. These tests rely on accurate and robust data acquisition systems (DAQ) to capture high-quality acceleration data. However, commercial DAQs that provide the required performance and features are often expensive and complex, limiting their accessibility for small-scale research and experimental applications. This work presents the design and experimental validation of an affordable and in-house-developed acceleration DAQ, tested on a small fixed-wing UAV through several Taxi Vibration Test (TVT) runs and ambient vibration measurements. The proposed system integrates several OrangePi 3 LTS single-board computers with multiple LSM6DS3TR-C MEMS inertial measurement units operating simultaneously via an Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C) communication interface, managed under a Python-based master/slave architecture. Data is acquired at a stable sampling rate of approximately 208 Hz and post-processed using Welch's method to estimate their Power Spectral Density (PSD). Results confirm the system ability to provide consistent multi-sensor acceleration data and repeatable PSD profiles under the same test conditions; thus, demonstrating its reliability. With a total hardware cost below 600 EUR (approximately 690 USD), the developed DAQ offers a compact, scalable and cost-effective alternative for aerospace vibration analysis and structural testing.

authors.name: Chaoyi Lin Yang, Gabriele Dessena, Oscar E. Bonilla-Manrique

papers.title: Modal Parameter Extraction via Propeller-Driven Vibration Testing
papers.summary: Ground Vibration Testing (GVT) supports aircraft certification but often requires lengthy and costly campaigns. Propeller-driven Vibration Testing (PVT) is assessed here as an output-only alternative, in line with Operational Modal Analysis approaches such as Taxi Vibration Testing and Flight Vibration Testing. A cantilever Aluminium 7075-T6 wing spar is instrumented with seven accelerometers and excited by an outboard electric motor and propeller. Seven runs are carried out: a motor-off baseline, five constant-throttle cases, and a manual up-down throttle sweep. The acquired spectra indicate that the dominant resonances remain observable under propeller excitation, while low-throttle conditions introduce narrowband harmonics that may mask structural peaks; the sweep reduces persistent overlap. Modal parameters are identified for the baseline and sweep cases using the Natural Excitation Technique with the Loewner Framework (NExT-LF). The first two modes remain closely matched (Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC) > 0.99), whereas the third mode shows reduced repeatability (MAC = 0.827) and a larger frequency shift, consistent with propeller-induced bending--torsion coupling and non-ideal sweep control. Overall, PVT provides a viable complement to GVT for extracting low-frequency modal information and motivates pursuing future work on automated throttle scheduling and coupling-aware test planning.

authors.name: Gabriele Dessena, Alessandro Pontillo

papers.title: End-to-End Multi-Task Learning for Adjustable Joint Noise Reduction and Hearing Loss Compensation
papers.summary: A multi-task learning framework is proposed for optimizing a single deep neural network (DNN) for joint noise reduction (NR) and hearing loss compensation (HLC). A distinct training objective is defined for each task, and the DNN predicts two time-frequency masks. During inference, NR and HLC can be adjusted independently by exponentiating each mask before combining them. In contrast to recent approaches that rely on training an auditory-model emulator to define a differentiable training objective, we propose an auditory model that is inherently differentiable, thus allowing end-to-end optimization. The audiogram is provided as an input to the DNN, thereby enabling listener-specific personalization without the need for retraining. Results show that the proposed approach not only allows adjusting NR and HLC independently, but also improves objective metrics compared with optimizing a single training objective. It also outperforms a cascade of two DNNs separately trained for NR and HLC and shows competitive HLC performance against a traditional hearing-aid prescription on objective metrics. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that uses an auditory model to train a single DNN for both NR and HLC across a wide range of flat and high-frequency-sloping hearing-loss profiles.

authors.name: Philippe Gonzalez, Vera Margrethe Frederiksen, Torsten Dau, Tobias May

papers.title: The Intrinsic Inertia, Droop, and Nonlinear Stability of Observer-Synchronized Grid-Forming Control
papers.summary: Observer-synchronized (OBS) grid-forming (GFM) control, in which grid synchronization, active-power regulation, voltage-magnitude regulation, and current limiting are integrated into a unified observer-based structure, was proposed in recent years as an alternative to conventional GFM control such as droop control. Existing research on OBS GFM mainly focuses on its linearized modelling, small-signal stability, and parameter sensitivity, while a nonlinear analysis, which characterizes its inertia, droop characteristics, and nonlinear convergence, is currently absent. This paper develops a systematic nonlinear analysis of OBS control. First, a second-order nonlinear autonomous model is derived under the quasi-steady-state assumption. The intrinsic inertia is characterized through an exact nonlinear swing-equation representation, while the nonlinear droop characteristics are derived from the steady-state relations. These results provide guidelines for controller parameterization. Furthermore, the equilibrium points and nonlinear stability properties are investigated using the qualitative theory of differential equations, giving explicit criteria to guarantee almost global asymptotic stability of the desired equilibriums. The analysis is validated through detailed electromagnetic transient simulations and hardware experiments.

authors.name: Aizuo Chen, Xiangyu Meng, Haozhe Wang, Boxin Liu, Yue Zhu

papers.title: Learning-Driven Channel Representation for Wireless Localization: From Channel Observations to Location Inference
papers.summary: Wireless observations capture radio signal responses formed through interactions with propagation environments and spatial geometry. In integrated sensing and communication, such observations have become an important basis for high-accuracy localization beyond conventional channel estimation. Learning-driven methods learn implicit relations between channel propagation and spatial position, enabling location inference under complex channel conditions. However, the useful information is tightly coupled with spatial layout, environmental dynamics, and system configurations. This coupling obscures the inference process and weakens performance consistency across scenarios. In this paper, we review learning-driven high-accuracy localization techniques with channel representations as the organizing view. The survey covers typical channel observation forms and analyzes their physical meanings. We also review channel feature extraction and representation learning methods, and summarize methods according to the acquisition, organization, adaptation, and reuse of channel representations. Typical methods are compared in terms of accuracy, applicable conditions, data requirements, and generalization. We model the localization process as a unified ``wireless observation--channel representation--location inference'' framework and use information bottleneck theory to highlight that the quality and usability of channel representations are critical to exploiting propagation information and play a decisive role in localization performance. Finally, we summarize the key challenges in moving from experimental studies to real deployment and present our perspectives on these issues.

authors.name: Hongyu Xie, Chenglong Li, Xinming Huang, Emmeric Tanghe, David Plets, Wout Joseph, Shaojie Ni, Xiaojun Yuan

papers.title: Techno-Economic Boundary Analysis of Small Modular Reactor Cogeneration for Hyperscale Data Center IT and Cooling Loads
papers.summary: Growing data-center electricity demand has increased interest in colocation with small modular reactors, but the conditions under which reactor power and steam-driven cooling reduce energy costs remain uncertain. Cooling can account for 20-40% of facility electricity use, making steam extraction a potential source of savings as well as a loss of turbine generation. We co-optimize hourly reactor dispatch, steam extraction, absorption cooling and grid exchange for a 200 MW$_\mathrm{e}$ data center in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) region, using a 109-entry scenario set spanning capital, market, policy, financing and cooling efficiency. At 2023 mid-range reactor capital, the nuclear configurations cost 54.9-67.7% more than grid supply even with the Section 45Y production tax credit. With the other 2023 assumptions held fixed, cogeneration reaches grid parity near \$5000 kW$_\mathrm{e}^{-1}$. At nth-of-a-kind capital, nuclear supply is 85.9-98.7% cheaper than grid procurement in 2023, but between parity and 34.8% more expensive in the low-price 2024 market. A carbon price of \$53.1-64.0 tCO$_2^{-1}$ closes the mid-range gap when exports receive credits at the hourly average grid emission factor; the resulting negative balances are attributional and do not represent physical carbon removal. Absorption cooling responds to hourly electricity prices and supplies 32.6% of annual cooling, but adds \$9.7 million yr$^{-1}$ relative to the reactor-only plant. Absorption breaks even at an installed cost of \$26 kW$_\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ at baseline efficiency and \$529 kW$_\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ on a legacy-efficiency campus, compared with surveyed commercial prices of \$450-1200 kW$_\mathrm{c}^{-1}$.

authors.name: Honglin Li, Buxin She, Jie Zhang

papers.title: Graph-Native Attention Acceleration for Attack Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.summary: Cyber-physical systems (CPSs) rely on extensive networks of sensors, controllers, and actuators, making them highly vulnerable to attacks targeting measurements, control logic, and equipment operations. While graph-based attack detectors, especially graph attention models, efficiently localize such attacks by exploiting the communication and physical interaction graphs. The computational cost of edge-wise attention scales poorly with the number of interactions. This bottleneck severely limits the scalability of online monitoring in large or densely connected CPSs. To address this challenge, we introduce GraphGHHA, a graph-native attention acceleration layer designed to reduce the inference cost of graph attention mechanisms in CPS security. GraphGHHA consists of a local attention unit (LAU) and a global attention unit (GAU). The LAU captures the local interactions by restricting the attention computation of each node of a CPS to a limited number of its neighbors, whereas the GAU captures the system-wide interactions. Dynamic gates then weight and combine these local and global representations. We evaluate GraphGHHA on a networked heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) cyber-physical system under representative attack scenarios. Based on our results, the inference latency of GraphGHHA is 89.3\% smaller than that of the standard graph attention layers (for an interaction graph size of 1536), while achieving an accuracy of 0.982 in detecting attacks. These results demonstrate that the proposed attention mechanism can significantly reduce the attack detection latency without compromising accuracy.

authors.name: Zhenan Feng, Ehsan Nekouei

papers.title: Impedance-Aware Optimized Pulse Patterns for Reconfigurable Battery Systems
papers.summary: Reconfigurable battery systems (RBS) synthesize the converter output voltage by inserting and bypassing battery cell groups, so every switching state changes not only the source voltage but also the source impedance. This paper shows that this configuration-dependent impedance breaks a tacit assumption of optimized pulse patterns (OPP): patterns designed with the customary linear plant model overestimate their achievable current quality by up to an order of magnitude and converge to a distortion floor set by the resistance modulation. We propose impedance-aware optimized pulse patterns (IA-OPP), which embed the level-dependent source impedance in the optimization objective, combined with an event-budget formulation that treats the reconfiguration rate of the communication bus as a managed resource. An exact closed-form evaluation of the piecewise-exponential load current renders the objective smooth in the switching instants. In a simulated cascaded-bridge reference system, IA-OPP attains 0.52% current total harmonic distortion (THD) at a reconfiguration rate of 2.4 kHz, outperforming nearest-level modulation, phase-shifted carrier pulse-width modulation (PWM) at up to five times the switching rate, and a classical OPP baseline at every event budget; the advantage persists across the modulation-index range and under +-30% parameter mismatch. For three-wire star-connected systems, masking triplen orders in the objective restores the full advantage, with the impedance-aware patterns beating their linear-model counterparts by about 20% at equal budget.

authors.name: Julian Estaller, Johannes Buberger, Andreas Wiedenmann, Wolfgang Grupp, Tobias Hoegerl, Thomas Weyh

papers.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC
papers.summary: This paper studies waveform-level security for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). Instead of relying on spatial beamforming or power allocation, we randomize the sensing waveform itself using phase keys and tangent Artificial Noise (AN) applied to a Fourier-curve constellation. Coordinated legitimate nodes know the key and recover the sensing reference, while Eve observes only a randomized waveform and cannot construct the correct coherent matched reference. We consider an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-mounted Eve with a dominant Line-of-Sight (LOS) link who fully exploits favorable geometry, including a bypass scenario where Eve listens to both the direct and echo sides to circumvent our design. We further consider a stronger Eve that attempts phase-key reconstruction from long-term observations; even then, residual key mismatch structurally degrades correlation and AN cancellation, while accurate key recovery incurs high computational complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed design reduces Eve's probability of detecting the sensing reference using non-coherent detection and, in the bypass case, substantially suppresses her correct-delay lock probability, while the legitimate receiver reliably locks onto the reference through echo accumulation.

authors.name: Zexin Fang, Bin Han, Shuangyang Li, Hans D. Schotten

papers.title: Every minute counts: Wind farm power control during imbalance settlement using distributional soft actor-critic
papers.summary: Wind farms can provide flexibility by curtailing their output during periods of excess generation in the power grid. One way to achieve this is through implicit balancing, where curtailment is performed in anticipation of a negative imbalance price. By doing so, the wind farm helps reduce system imbalance while also lowering its own costs. However, implicit balancing is challenging, since imbalance prices are hard to predict and can also be affected by the control actions taken by the farm. To address both challenges, we use distributional soft actor-critic (distSAC) to learn a control policy that adjusts the power setpoint every minute. Using real data of the Belgian grid and an offshore wind farm, we show that our method can turn the imbalance costs caused by forecast errors into a small revenue. Moreover, distSAC outperforms a price threshold controller, often used in industry, and performs slightly better than soft actor-critic (SAC). Unlike SAC, distSAC can also learn risk-averse policies by optimizing a risk measure, such as conditional value at risk. These risk-averse policies were found to better account for their price impact, reducing overshoots by 16-27% while achieving similar cost savings. Last, we find that 1-minute setpoints lead to lower imbalance costs than 15-minute setpoints, regardless of the control policy.

authors.name: Max Bruninx, Seyed Soroush Karimi Madahi, Timothy Verstraeten, Jan Decuyper, Chris Develder, Ann Now\'e, Jan Helsen

papers.title: Decoding Motion-Blurred QR Codes: Motion-Parameter Error Tolerance and Model-Based Recovery
papers.summary: In automated manufacturing, logistics, and inspection, Quick Response (QR) codes are often read on the fly under continuous ambient light without active strobes or motion pauses. The resulting relative three-dimensional motion produces spatially varying blur that defeats standard decoders, yet how accurately the motion must be estimated to recover the payload remains an open question. To address this question from a task-driven evaluation perspective centered on machine recognition effectiveness, we formulate motion-blurred QR recovery within a unified mathematical framework of identifiability. Within this framework, we systematically measure the decoding tolerance to perturbations in motion length, direction, rotation or scaling centre, and speed profile. These controlled experiments reveal three structural laws: 1) parameter tolerances shrink rapidly as blur amplitude grows and are tightest under uniform speed, whereas accelerating motion is substantially more forgiving; 2) length tolerance can differ markedly between underestimation and overestimation; 3) errors that are individually benign interact strongly and prevent decoding when combined. Guided by these findings, we propose a grey-box recovery pipeline in which two compact networks predict an initial corner trajectory, followed by tolerance-guided candidate search, alternating image-and-path fitting, and regularised linear inversion. On a benchmark of 955 real motion-blurred photographs spanning four camera models and four rigid-motion families, our method recovers the exact payload on 93.1% of the images. It outperforms the strongest fine-tuned deblurring network at 83.6% and reduces the decoding error rate by 58.0%, with zero wrong strings accepted.

authors.name: Zhi Zeng, Qiaochen Su, Si Xiong, Yaoqi Wang, Yufei Cai, Heng Liu, Yi Hu

papers.title: Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Neural Optimal Control
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a prominent data-driven approach to optimal control, but suffers from sample inefficiency and sensitivity to the data distribution. In this paper, we propose an alternative approach grounded in the well-established Hamilton-Jacobi framework in optimal control theory. Rather than requiring an explicit analytical model of the system dynamics to evaluate the Hamiltonian, we replace this with a Data-Driven Hamiltonian (DDH) that can be applied to a broad class of optimal control problems. In contrast to standard RL approaches, the DDH provides a principled mechanism for quantifying and accounting for uncertainty in regions not covered by the data, requiring only minimal prior system information such as a Lipschitz constant. Additional prior system knowledge, when available, can be readily incorporated to improve performance. For higher-dimensional systems, we further introduce a physics-informed neural approximation of the value function, trained using a novel procedure that generates worst-case fictitious rollouts from the DDH. On an LQR problem, the DDH reaches near-optimal cost on every dataset we test, including random data on which offline RL methods remain far from optimal, and needs far fewer samples than online RL. On a nonlinear lunar lander benchmark, the DDH achieves an optimality gap relative to a trajectory-optimization reference that is less than one-third of those achieved by CQL and FQL, while matching SAC's performance with approximately $37\times$ fewer samples.

authors.name: Christopher A. Strong, Aswin Surya, Namhoon Cho, Jason J. Choi, Claire J. Tomlin

papers.title: Lie Group Structure of Six-Degree-of-Freedom Rigid-Body Uncertainty Representation and Propagation
papers.summary: For six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body motion, the choice of Lie-group structure affects both how well the group-theoretic mean and covariance represent the state distribution and how accurately these moments are propagated. A quaternion-based, left-trivialized semidirect-product formulation of the velocity phase space is developed for the actuated body-frame dynamics, with closed-form group operations and Jacobians that avoid matrix-group embeddings. We derive the controlled stochastic dynamics and establish that the direct- and semidirect-product formulations describe the same physical process under the specified noise model. Since the semidirect exponential coordinates account for frame changes between body twists at different poses, they capture pose--twist coupling more naturally. A lunar powered-descent experiment assesses low-order moment representations of uncertainty and propagation performance under the proposed group structure using two distinct algorithms. Compared with direct-product formulations and a linearized baseline, the proposed structure improves the representation of the banana-shaped body-velocity distribution using group-theoretic moments, yields more consistent propagated moments, and produces distribution approximations that agree more closely with the Monte Carlo reference. In this experiment, changing the group structure accounts for most of the observed improvement, highlighting the practical value of the proposed semidirect-product formulation.

authors.name: Zhuochen Wang, Panagiotis Tsiotras

papers.title: Social Welfare and Equilibrium in Distributed Microgrid Prosumer Coordination Under a Mixed Competitive-Cooperative Setting
papers.summary: Price-based distributed prosumer coordination in distribution networks is fundamentally challenging when the aggregator pursues grid-level goals that couple prosumers' decisions, because the Lagrangian fails to separate and nodal prices are undefined under conventional dual decomposition. This paper develops a novel method that embeds mixed competitive-cooperative objectives exactly into prices, which are split into energy, congestion, and grid-objective components, closing the gap between the social welfare optimum and the competitive equilibrium. To compute the equilibrium, a distributed optimization algorithm is developed based on the projected Arrow-Hurwicz-Uzawa scheme. Explicit step-size rules are developed for the algorithm to guarantee $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{L})$ and $\mathcal{O}(1/L)$ ergodic convergence rates. Simulations on an IEEE 33-bus feeder that is connected to prosumers and electric vehicle fleets validate the accuracy and efficacy of the proposed methods.

authors.name: Mahan Fakourifard, Elizabeth L. Ratnam, Mingxi Liu

papers.title: ASDL: A Fast Vector Approximation Algorithm for Multiplierless Designs of Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.summary: Matrix multiplications are one of the main computational bottlenecks in neural networks. The calculation reduces to numerous sums of partial products, which scale with the total number of Signed Power of Two (SPT) values in the multiplier matrix. Minimizing the SPT count can significantly reduce the computational burden. In this context, we present a Sum Of (signed) Powers Of Two (SOPOT) vector approximation algorithm that limits SPT counts, namely the Accelerated Signed Digit Loading (ASDL) algorithm. This approximation algorithm converts ResNet50 10 times faster than its predecessor MPGBP, while being more precise. We apply this method to the pre-trained coefficients of different convolutional neural networks, achieving 80.41\% ImageNet accuracy down from 81.3\%, at an average of only 1.5 active bits per coefficient. This is done without any retraining or calibration, which are typically required for the most aggressive quantization methods. Our approach offers a promising direction for neural network inference with higher energy efficiency and fewer hardware requirements: we anticipate up to 10 times improvement over bfloat16 inference.

authors.name: Guillaume H. Tong, Luiz F. da S. Coelho, Lounis Zerioul, Didier Le Ruyet

papers.title: Blind Deconvolution of Nonstationary Graph Signals over Shift-Invariant Channels
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the blind deconvolution of nonstationary graph signals from noisy observations transmitted through an unknown shift-invariant channel, under the assumption that the covariance structure of the source signals is known to the observer. Based on a phase retrieval framework, we develop a method to estimate the unknown channel and subsequently recover the source signals via frequency-domain Wiener filtering. We derive theoretical error bounds for both the proposed channel estimation and the resulting blind deconvolution. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through numerical experiments on cycle graphs and a real-world temperature dataset collected in the Brest region of France.

authors.name: Ali Zare, Yao Shi, Qiyu Sun

papers.title: Reducing the Power Required for Multi-UAV Tethered Payload Transportation via a Rotating Equilibrium
papers.summary: Collaborative aerial transportation of tethered payloads is fundamentally limited by space, power, and weight constraints. Conventional approaches rely on static equilibrium conditions, where each vehicle tilts to generate the forces that ensure they maintain a formation geometry that avoids aerodynamic interactions and collision. This horizontal thrust component represents a significant energy penalty compared to the ideal case in which each vehicle produces purely vertical thrust to lift the payload. Operating in tighter tether configurations can minimize this effect, but at the cost of either having to fly the vehicles in closer proximity, which risks collision, or significantly increasing the length of the tether, which increases complexity and reduces potential use-cases. We propose operating the tether-suspended flying system at a rotating equilibrium. By maintaining steady circular motion, centrifugal forces provide the necessary horizontal tether tension, allowing each quadrotor to generate purely vertical thrust and thus reducing the total force (and power) required compared to an equilibrium where the thrusts are not vertical. It also allows for a wider range of tether configurations to be used without sacrificing efficiency. Results demonstrate that rotating equilibria can reduce power consumption relative to static lifting by up to 20%, making collaborative aerial solutions more practically relevant.

authors.name: Eric Foss, Andrew Tai, Carlo Bosio, Mark W. Mueller

papers.title: SPROUT: The Open-Source Soft Growing Robot for Search and Rescue
papers.summary: Soft robotic systems have long been theorized as ideal candidates for use in search and rescue operations; however, there have been significant barriers to entry in graduating soft robotic systems from the laboratory to the field. To address this gap in replicable, reliable soft robot systems, we present the designs for SPROUT, the Soft Pathfinding Robotic Observation Unit. The system has matured over years of interaction with professional urban search and rescue communities, with the goal of operating in dusty, wet, and isolated conditions. This manuscript contains supplementary material, including code, parts manifests, CAD assemblies, and build instructions to allow the broader robotics research community to build their own SPROUT systems. The modular hardware and ROS 2-based software stack support task-specific payloads and control functions, allowing SPROUT to be adapted for applications beyond search and rescue, including infrastructure inspection and archaeology. Here, we demonstrate SPROUT performing a variety of challenging inspection and traversal tasks in collapsed structure training sites used by first responders. The main project page is available online at https://sprout-mitll.github.io/sprout/.

authors.name: Antonio Alvarez Valdivia, Ciera McFarland, Robert Reeve, Ankush Dhawan, Chad Council, Megan Richardson, Margaret McGuinness, Nathaniel Hanson

papers.title: On the parametric and semiparametric Fisher information matrix for non-zero mean stationary spherical invariant random processes
papers.summary: The classical Whittle formula provides a closed-form expression for the asymptotic Fisher information matrix (FIM) rate of multidimensional, real-valued, zero-mean, purely nondeterministic stationary Gaussian processes (GPs), expressed in terms of their parameterized spectra within a maximum-likelihood framework. However, the Gaussian assumption underlying this result restricts its applicability to many real-world signals exhibiting heavy-tailed or non-Gaussian behavior. In this paper, we extend Whittle's result to multidimensional, real-valued stationary compound Gaussian processes (CGPs) with arbitrary mean, under a unified framework encompassing fully known, parameterized, and completely unknown density generators. Building upon the Slepian-Bangs formula for $n$ consecutive observations and extending it to the semiparametric setting, we leverage the asymptotic properties of block Toeplitz matrices to obtain a closed-form spectral-domain expression for the asymptotic FIM rate. The resulting expression, common to all density generator families, generalizes the standard zero-mean Gaussian formula by incorporating a distribution-dependent contribution associated with the nonzero mean, and an additional covariance term that is invariant to the choice of non-Gaussian distribution. This extension enables efficient and theoretically grounded performance analysis for heavy-tailed signal processing applications.

authors.name: Jean-Pierre Delmas, Habti Abeida, Stefano Fortunati

papers.title: K-subareas partitioning subject to coinciding boundary segments of neighboring subareas
papers.summary: A method for the problem of partitioning an area into K subareas subject to coinciding boundary segments of neighboring subareas is presented. The given area may be non-convex and may additionally include obstacle areas. The proposed hierarchical method involves three steps: repeated bisection splitting, merging and the solution of traveling salesman problems. Geographic real-world outdoors areas data is used for the evaluation of the method. The benefit of computational simplicity at the cost of imbalanced subarea sizes is highlighted.

authors.name: Mogens Plessen
